en: Now begins the fifty-first chapter: On Sub-periods (Antardaśā).
The ten-year periods, multiplied by their respective measures and divided by the sum of all [periods], yield the individual sub-periods (antardaśās);
likewise, the sub-sub-periods (pratyantardaśās) and so forth are calculated. || 1 ||
At the beginning, the sub-period (antardaśā) of the lord of the main period (pākapati) occurs first, and the others follow in that sequence;
thus, the wise should understand this order applies at the start of every sub-sub-period (pratyantaradaśā) as well.
The enjoyment (bhukti) of the nine planets shall be equal; the period (daśā) is to be divided into nine parts.
First is the enjoyment of the lord of the period, followed by those [planets] conjoined with its angles (kendras) and so forth. (3)

One should understand the subtle periods (daśās) and so forth according to the sequence of the portions of enjoyment; the wise should declare the results according to the order of strength, following the previously mentioned method. ||4||
Having established the solar year as the period of the zodiac signs, one should state the motion of each sign in due order;
having performed this for every sub-period (antardaśā) and so forth, one should declare their respective results.
Between the first and the seventh [houses], whichever sign is strongest—
from that point, the periods (daśās) are to be counted in direct order if the house of the period is odd, and in reverse order if it is even.

O twice-born one, there is another distinction here which I shall tell you: in a movable sign, one should practice without abandoning the path; in a fixed sign, it should be every sixth meal, and so forth.

Both types of thorns (kaṇṭaka) are to be known from the ascendant, the fifth house, and the ninth house; the sequence is considered to be first in odd signs of the movable (cara), fixed (sthira), and dual-natured (dvisvabhāva) classes. 8.
From those same three pairs, everything should be taken in reverse order;
thus the heap is delineated, and the heap of cooked [results] is declared.
That very same mass of enjoyments is recorded as occurring in the first cycle;
it is seen in whichever cycle the maturation of the [karma] from the first [house] occurs at a specific ordinal position.
Therefore, let the enjoyment corresponding to that [lot] be taken there in the turn;
this applies to both the mobile turn and the fixed turn. (11)
In the period known as the Trikoṇa (Trine), the determination of the ripening and enjoyment [of results] occurs;
when both the ripening and enjoyment are abundant with malefic planets, there is affliction from the king and suffering from the head.
Now I shall describe the method for the sub-periods within the composite period (piṇḍatrikadaśā):
the lord of the full period shall grant [its duration], and half of that, joined with it, [is granted by the others]. (13)

A planet situated in a trine gains a third part [of its strength], one in a square gains a fourth part, and one in the seventh house gains a seventh part; among many, the single planet is the strongest. (14)
In this manner, the planets situated together digest one another;
provided they have been reduced to equal degrees and are not subtracted from one another. (15)
The ten-year periods, multiplied by their respective degrees and divided by the sum of the degrees, become the sub-periods (antardaśās);
in this same manner, the sub-sub-periods (pratyantardaśās) and so forth are determined.
Now begins the chapter on the results of the sub-periods within the periods of the Sun according to the Viṃśottarī system. || 52 ||

The Sun situated in its exaltation or its own sign, in the eleventh house, a quadrant, or a trine, brings gains of wealth, grain, and other riches during its own major period and its own sub-period. || 1 ||
If the Sun is situated in a base or inauspicious sign, it shall bestow contrary results;
if the Sun is the lord of the second or the seventh house, one should predict the fear of untimely death.
To avoid those defects, one should perform the recitation of the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra;
one should perform a propitiatory rite (śānti) to please the Sun for the sake of attaining health.
When the Moon is within the Sun's course and situated in a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant, it brings about marriage, auspicious undertakings, and the prosperity of wealth and grain. (4)

There will be the expansion of houses and fields, as well as abundance of livestock and vehicles; moreover, when [the Moon] is in its exaltation or its own sign, there will be happiness from one's wife and the arrival of wealth. || 5 ||
Through the grace of the Great King, there shall be the happiness of obtaining a son, the joy of meeting with the king, and the attainment of desired success, which brings forth bliss.
Or when [the moon] is waned or conjoined with malefic planets, there is suffering for one's wife, children, and others;
discord among people, and the destruction of one's circle of servants. (7)
If the Moon is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, there will be conflict, strife with the king, loss of wealth, grain, and cattle, fear of water, and mental affliction.
It brings about bondage, the affliction of disease, displacement from one's position,
an unfavorable situation, and mental conflict with kinsmen.
One should indicate contemptible food, as well as oppression by thieves and the like or by the king; furthermore, there will be urinary disorders, abdominal diseases, and bodily affliction. (10)

If the lord of the eighth house is in the ninth or tenth house, or in a quadrant (kendr), conjoined with a benefic, it bestows enjoyment, fortune, contentment, and the increase of wife, children, and so forth. || 11 ||
The attainment of a kingdom, great happiness, and the acquisition of an eternal station; marriage, initiation for sacrifice, beautiful garlands, and celestial ornaments.

One obtains vehicles, sons, grandsons, and so forth, which increase happiness, when the lord of the Dasa is situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa, or is devoid of strength. (13)

If the lord of the second house is in its depression, there will be eating at improper times and wandering from place to place; furthermore, there will be untimely death (apamṛtyu). To attain happiness, one should give a white cow or a buffalo and perform propitiatory rites (śānti).

When Mars is within the period of the Sun, situated in its exaltation, its own sign, or its house of gain, or in a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant, one should predict auspicious affairs. || 15 ||

It brings gain from the earth and gain from agriculture, the increase of wealth and grain, the acquisition of houses, fields, and the like, and the obtaining of red garments and other such items. || 16 ||

If [the Moon] is conjoined with the lord of the ascendant, one should declare happiness and favor from the king; if conjoined with the lords of the ninth or eleventh houses, there will surely be gain. (17)
He will possess the command of a vast army, the destruction of enemies, and a firm mind;
he will have happiness from his own kin and likewise bring prosperity to his brothers.
If the lord of the eighth house is situated in the twelfth house from the lord of the ascendant, conjoined with or aspected by malefics,
and devoid of the strength of lordship, it causes a cruel disposition and mental anguish.
And it foretells entry into prison, the destruction of kinsmen, discord with brothers, or even the failure of one's undertakings. (20)
If Mars is in its sign of debilitation or weak, there is loss of wealth due to the king;
if the lord of the second or seventh house is so situated, there is dullness of body and mental affliction.
One should likewise perform the Subrahmaṇya-japa and the release of a bull,
as well as a peace-rite (śānti) performed according to rule, which bestows the attainment of long life and health.
When Rāhu enters the period of the Sun and is situated in a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant, there will be loss of wealth and great fear for the first two months. (23)
There is fear of thieves and the like, as well as wounds, and suffering for one's wife and children;
yet thereafter, one attains happiness when [the planet] is joined with a benefic and situated in a benefic division (aṃśaka). || 24 ||
When Rāhu is in an Upacaya house from the Lagna and is conjoined with a Yoga-kāraka, there is bodily health, mental contentment, and happiness that wins the favor of the king. (25)

If [the Moon] is situated in the sixth house from the lord of the Dasa, one should predict honor from the king, an increase in fortune, the attainment of fame, and suffering for wife, children, and others. (26)

The joy of a son’s festival and other such auspicious glories in the home [occur] when [the lord of the year] is situated in the twelfth or the eighth house from the lord of the dasa, being devoid of strength. (27)
There will be imprisonment, loss of position, confinement in a prison cell, fear of wounds from thieves and the like, and the increase of wife, children, and other dependents. (28)

There will be the loss of four-footed animals, the destruction of houses, fields, and so forth, as well as diseases such as tumors and consumption, and the affliction of dysentery and other ailments. (29)
Likewise, when Rāhu is situated in Dvispashṭa and conjoined with the lord of that house,
there arises both the fear of untimely death and the danger from serpents.
One should perform the recitation of the Durgā-mantra and practice the gift of safety;
one should give a black cow or a buffalo, and thereby attains the end [of suffering] without doubt. || 31 ||
When Jupiter is within the period of the Sun, situated in a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant,
in its own exaltation, or in the division of a friend, there occurs marriage and an audience with the king.

Through the favor of the great king, there shall be the acquisition of wealth, grain, and so forth, the birth of a son, and great happiness; it brings about the attainment of desired goals and purposes. (33)

O twice-born one, one should predict the acquisition of royal power through the influence of the lord of fortune and karma, as well as the favor of Brahmins, respect from the virtuous, and the gain of beloved garments and other such things.
There is the yoga of being carried by men, an abundance of status, and great happiness;
when [the Moon] is in the third house from the lord of the Dasa, there is an increase in fortune that brings comfort. (35)

Engaged in humble religious practices, devoted to the propitiation of the deities, possessing devotion to the guru and mental perfection, he accumulates merit through virtuous deeds and the like. (36)
If the lord of the [ascendant] sign is situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, or is debilitated, or conjoined with malefic planets,
there will be suffering for the wife, children, and others, as well as bodily affliction and great fear.
It causes royal wrath, the destruction of desired objects, the loss of wealth rooted in sin, physical decline, and mental anguish. (38)
One should perform the gift of gold and have one's own desired mantra recited;
by the gift of tawny-colored cows, one should prescribe the attainment of health.

When Saturn enters the period of the Sun and occupies a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant, it causes the destruction of enemies, great happiness, and the acquisition of small amounts of grain and wealth. (40)
And auspicious ceremonies such as marriage will bring good fortune in his home, when Saturn is in its exaltation, its own sign, or conjoined with a friendly planet. (41)

In the home, there shall be an abundance of auspicious prosperity, the performance of virtuous rites such as marriages and the like, honor from kings, renown, and the acquisition of various garments and wealth. (42)
If the lord of the eighth house is situated in the eighth or the twelfth house from the lord of the year, or is conjoined with malefic planets,
there will be suffering from wind-related colic, major diseases, fever, and dysentery.
Imprisonment, failure in one's undertakings, loss of wealth, great fear, sudden quarrels, and conflict with kinsmen shall occur. (44)

At the beginning of its period, there will be loss of friends; in the middle, it brings some happiness; and at the end, it causes distress. The same applies to those planets when they are in their sign of debilitation.
There will be separation from father and mother, as well as constant coming and going;
if the lord of the second house is deficient, there shall be fear of untimely death.
One should give a black cow as a mahiṣī gift, perform the recitation of the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra,
and make the gift of a sword, which bestows all prosperity.

When Mercury is situated within the mouth of the Sun, or is in its exaltation, or even in its own sign, and is placed in a quadrant, a trine, or the eleventh house, endowed with the strength of its various divisions (varga-balas); || 48 ||

There is the attainment of a kingdom, great enthusiasm, and the bringing of happiness through wife, sons, and so forth; by the grace of a great king, one obtains vehicles, garments, and ornaments. (49)

When [the Moon] is joined with the lords of fortune (bhāgya) and gain (lābha), there shall be the attainment of the fruits of sacred pilgrimage sites at home, an abundance of cattle wealth, and the increase of profit.
When the fifth house from the ascendant (the house of fortune) is occupied by Mars, honor is certain;
there is also a virtuous inclination toward righteous deeds, as well as devotion to teachers, gods, and the twice-born.

When the lord of the Dasa is situated in the fourth house from the Lagna and is joined by a benefic planet, there occurs marriage accompanied by wealth, grain, and the like, as well as the birth of a son; there is great happiness.
In marriage rites, sacrificial ceremonies, acts of charity, religious duties, recitations, and so forth, one should employ verses inscribed with one's own name, or even both names. (53)

A man shall obtain food, clothing, ornaments, and wealth and become a lord among the immortals, even if [the planet] is situated in the sixth, seventh, or twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa, or is in its sign of debilitation. (54)

Physical affliction, mental anguish, and suffering caused by wife, children, and so forth—he experiences such pain at the beginning of enjoyment; in the middle, it brings only a slight measure of pleasure. (55)
In the first [period], there is fear of the king as well as constant coming and going;
in the second, when the lord of the house is afflicted, there is stiffness of the body, fever, and so forth.
One should cause the recitation of the Thousand Names of Viṣṇu and the gift of food to be performed;
one should also make a gift of a silver image for the attainment of health.
When Ketu enters the period of the Sun, there is affliction of the body, mental anguish, expenditure of wealth, royal displeasure, and trouble from one's own kinsmen and others. || 58 ||
If [the Moon] is conjoined with the lord of the ascendant, there is happiness and the arrival of wealth at first;
in the middle [of the period], one encounters distress from that, and one should predict the arrival of news of death.
Likewise, if [the lord of the eighth house] is conjoined with a malefic planet from the lord of the Dāya in the eighth house,
there will be diseases of the cheeks and teeth, as well as the occurrence of urinary disorders.
Loss of position, loss of wealth, the death of a father, departure to a foreign land, affliction by enemies, and great fear [shall occur]. (61)
When Ketu is in an Upacaya house from the Ascendant, conjoined with a Yoga-kāraka, and situated in a benefic Navamsha and a benefic Varga, there arises the fruit of auspicious actions. || 62 ||
There shall be happiness from children, wife, and others, as well as contentment that increases what is dear;
there will be the acquisition of variegated garments and an increase in fame that brings joy. (63)
If the lord of the second house or any subsequent house is deficient [in strength], one should predict the fear of untimely death;
for the attainment of well-being, one should perform the recitation of the Durgā-mantra and the gift of a cow.

When Venus is within the period of the Sun, or is situated in a trine or a quadrant, or is in its own exaltation, in a friendly sign, or in its own division, there is the enjoyment of desired women and wealth. (65)
Traveling to another village, the sight of Brahmins and lords, the acquisition of a kingdom, great enthusiasm, and the splendor of the royal parasol and fly-whisk. (66)
In the house, there is an abundance of auspiciousness and the constant enjoyment of sweet foods;
there is the acquisition of gems such as coral, and the gaining of pearls, garments, and other such things.
There will be the acquisition of four-footed creatures, as well as abundant grain, wealth, and so forth; there will be enthusiasm, renown, prosperity, and the fortune of possessing human vehicles.

If Venus is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from the lord of the Mahadasha and is devoid of strength, there will be royal displeasure, mental distress, and the loss of sons, wife, and wealth. (69)

At the beginning of a journey and so forth, it is middling; in the middle, there will be gain that brings auspiciousness; but at the end, there is the destruction of fame or even the loss of one's position. (70)
One may speak with hatred toward kinsmen or suffer the loss of enjoyments from one's own family;
when Venus is the lord of the seventh house, there is dullness of body and fear of disease. (71)
If [the Moon] is conjoined with Rāhu or Venus, untimely death will surely occur;
to ward off that defect, one should perform the recitation of the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra. 72.
One should give a white cow or a buffalo and cause the recitation of the Rudra-mantra to be performed;
thereafter, one attains peace through the grace of Śaṅkara.
Now begins the chapter on the results of the sub-periods (antardaśā) of the Moon. || 53 ||

When the Moon is in its exaltation, its own sign, or in a trine or the eleventh house, and is conjoined with the lords of the ninth and tenth houses, there will be an abundance of elephants, horses, and garments. || 1 ||
Devotion to the deities and the guru, the chanting of the praises of those of virtuous fame, the acquisition of a kingdom, great happiness, and the increase of renown bring about well-being. (2)
When the moon is full, there is full strength, the position of commander-in-chief, and great happiness;
however, if the moon is conjoined with malefic planets, or is in its sign of debilitation, or situated in the eighth or sixth house, [the opposite occurs]. || 3 ||
At an improper time, there will be loss of wealth or perhaps displacement from one's position;
there will be physical ailments, mental anguish, and conflict with the king and his ministers.
There will be distress for the mother, mental anguish, imprisonment, and the loss of kinsmen, if the lord of the second house is conjoined with the lord of the eighth or twelfth house. || 5 ||
One should declare physical lethargy, great failure, and fear of untimely death;
one should give away a white cow or a buffalo when the Moon is within its own period.
When Mars is situated within the sign of the Moon and occupies a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant,
there is good fortune, honor from the king, and [the acquisition of] clothing, food, and ornaments.
Through effort, the accomplishment of one's purpose will surely come to pass; there is no doubt.
There shall be an increase in house and field, and victory in legal disputes.

There is attainment of one's purpose and great happiness when Mars is in its exaltation or its own sign; such is the result, provided Mars is not in the eighth or twelfth house, nor is it conjoined with malefic planets. || 9 ||
If an inauspicious planet occupies the eleventh house (dāyaśāda) and is aspected by another malefic, there will be physical suffering,
loss of houses, fields, and so forth, as well as failure in legal proceedings.
In the divisions of death, there will be quarrels, opposition from the king, separation from one's own kinsmen, and constant harsh speech. (11)
If the lord of the second house is in the eighth house, and the lord of the eighth house is [also] there,
one should perform the worship of a Brāhmaṇa for the sake of appeasing those two.

When Rāhu has entered into the Moon and is situated in a quadrant (kendram) or a trine (trikoṇa) from the ascendant, its results should be known at first to be meager; there will be affliction from enemies and great fear.
There shall be fear of thieves, snakes, and kings; suffering to four-footed creatures; loss of kinsmen, loss of friends, loss of honor, and mental anguish. (14)

When [a planet] is conjoined with benefics, aspected by benefics, or situated in a triplicity from the ascendant, and is connected to a yoga-maker (yogakāraka), it brings about the accomplishment of all undertakings and goals. || 15 ||
In the southwest and in the western state, there may be a meeting with one's lord at some time;
there will be the acquisition of vehicles and garments, and the accomplishment of one's desired tasks and goals. (16)

If the lord of the eighth house or the twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa is devoid of strength, there will be displacement from one's position, mental suffering, distress regarding sons, and great fear. || 17 ||
In some cases, suffering for one's wife should be known; in others, there is danger of pain in one's own limbs.
There is fear from the venom of scorpions and the like, as well as affliction caused by thieves, snakes, and kings. (18)

If [the lord of the eighth house] is in a quadrant, a trine, the twelfth, or the eleventh house from the lord of the year, there is the attainment of the fruits of holy pilgrimage sites and the great vision of deities. (19)
There will be an accumulation of meritorious deeds such as acts of helping others;
however, if the second or seventh house is afflicted, there will be physical suffering.
To avoid those defects, one should perform the recitation of the Rudra-mantra and practice the gift of medicine;
thus, health of the body is produced.

When Jupiter is within the sign of the Moon and situated in a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant, or in its own house, the eleventh house, or its exaltation, there is the attainment of a kingdom and a great festival. || 22 ||

The acquisition of garments, ornaments, and decorations, the favor of the king, the arrival of wealth, and through the grace of one's chosen deity, the fruition of rites such as the conception ceremony (garbhādhāna). || 23 ||
Likewise, auspicious undertakings, Lakṣmī casting her glances upon the home, wealth derived from royal patronage, and possession of land, elephants, and horses [are attained]. (24)

Through the favor of the great king, the accomplishment of one's own desires brings happiness, provided that Jupiter is not in its sign of debilitation or set, nor situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house. (25)
If it is conjoined with a malefic planet, there will be inauspicious karma, the destruction of the preceptor’s son and others, loss of position, mental distress, and certainly, sudden quarrels. (26)

There will be the destruction of houses, fields, and so forth, as well as the loss of vehicles and clothing, if [the planet] is in a quadrant (kendram), a trine (koṇam), the sixth house (duścikyam), or the eleventh house (lābhaga) from the lord of the period (dāyeśa). || 27 ||
It brings gain from food, clothing, and adversaries, as well as happiness;
it bestows the prosperity of joy from brothers and others, along with fortitude, vigor, and prowess. (28)

Sacrifices, vows, marriages, and so forth, as well as royal splendor and abundance of wealth, [are lost] when the lord of the Dasa is situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from the Lagna and is devoid of strength. (29)
It causes contemptuous food and likewise travel to foreign lands; it is said to be auspicious at the beginning of a meal, but it brings about distress at the end. (30)
If the lord of the second house is deficient, untimely death (apamṛtyu) will occur;
for the sake of averting that defect, one should recite the Śivasahasranāma.
It is declared that the gift of gold is the remover of all misfortunes.

When Saturn has entered the sign of the Moon and is situated in a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant, and when Saturn is in its own house, in its own division, and endowed with its exaltation degrees; || 32 ||
Or if the eleventh house is conjoined with a benefic aspect or endowed with strength,
there will be the attainment of sons, friends, and wealth through association with a Śūdra master.
From exertion comes an abundance of fruit; it bestows the increase of houses, fields, and so forth, as well as the gain of sons, auspiciousness, and the majesty of royal favor. (34)

When Saturn is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, or in its sign of debilitation, or even in the second house—at the commencement of its transit and so forth—there shall indeed be bathing at sacred pilgrimage sites and [auspicious] sightings. (35)

There will be terror among many people and suffering from weapons if [the Moon] is situated in a quadrant (kendrā) or a trine (trikoṇa) from the lord of the sub-period, even if it possesses strength. || 36 ||

In some cases there will be happiness and the acquisition of wealth, yet it will cause discord with one's wife and children; if [the planet] is situated in the second, seventh, or eighth house, there will be affliction to the body. (37)
To avoid those defects, one should perform the recitation of the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra;
one should give a black cow or a buffalo as a gift, and by this donation, one may predict good health.
When Mercury is situated within the sign of the Moon, occupying a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine;
or when Mercury is in its own sign, its own Navamsha, its exaltation, or endowed with strength. || 39 ||
The arrival of wealth brings about the acquisition of honors, beloved garments, and other such things;
it provides learning, recreation, and excellent companionship, while the increase of knowledge brings happiness. (40)
It brings about the acquisition of progeny or contentment, the gain of wealth through trade, and the obtaining of vehicles, umbrellas, and various ornaments. (41)

If [the lord of the year] is in a quadrant (kendraka), a trine (koṇa), the eleventh house, or even the second house from the lord of the year, there will be marriage, initiation for sacrifice (yajñadīkṣā), giving of gifts, religious duties, and other auspicious events. (42)
An assembly of learned men brings joy even to a king; likewise, pearls, gems, corals, vehicles, garments, and ornaments [are sources of delight]. (43)

Health, joy, and happiness, as well as the pleasure of drinking soma and other such delights, [are obtained] when [the Moon] is in the sixth, seventh, or eighth house from the lord of the dasa, or in the twelfth house, or even in its sign of debilitation. (44)
During its consumption, there is affliction of the body, destruction of crops, cattle, and land, as well as entry into prison and suffering for one's wife, children, and others. (45)
If the lord of the second house is deficient [of strength], there will be suffering from fever and great fear;
one should perform the gift of medicine and recite the Viṣṇusahasranāma.

When Ketu is situated within the Moon's sign and occupies a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine, and is endowed with strength in the second house, there is gain of wealth and great happiness. || 47 ||

He experiences happiness from children, wife, and so forth, and performs his prescribed duties; however, there will be loss of wealth at the beginning of the period of enjoyment, while he attains happiness when it is in its middle.

If [the lord of the year] is in a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine from the lord of the Dasa, and is endowed with strength, it will at times give results at the beginning of the period, such as happiness and the arrival of wealth. (49)
There will be the acquisition of cows, buffaloes, and so forth, but at the end of the period, there will be loss of wealth;
this occurs when [the planet] is joined with or aspected by malefics, or is situated in the eighth or twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa.
There will be loss of undertakings due to enemies and certainly sudden quarrels;
indeed, on that day, the second and seventh houses portend ill health and great fear. (51)
One should perform the recitation of the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra, which bestows all prosperity;
thereafter, one attains peace through the grace of Śaṅkara.
When Venus enters the sign of the Moon and is situated in a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine, or is in its exaltation or its own sign, it brings about the attainment of a kingdom. || 53 ||
Through the favor of the Great King, there shall be the acquisition of vehicles, garments, and ornaments;
the gain of four-footed animals, and the increase of wife, sons, and other kin. (54)
The construction of a new house, the constant eating of sweet foods, fragrant flowers and garlands, beautiful women, and the attainment of health; 55.
When joined with the lord of the period (daśādhipa), it brings physical comfort and great happiness;
it causes the increase of good fame, happiness, prosperity, houses, fields, and so forth. (56)
When Venus is in its debilitation or has set, and is conjoined with or aspected by malefic planets,
there is destruction of land, the loss of sons, friends, and others, and the death of the wife.
There will be loss of four-footed animals and the creation of enmity at the royal court;
yet, when Venus is situated in the second house, being in its own sign or conjoined with its own domicile, [these evils do not occur]. (58)
It brings the discovery of hidden treasure, great happiness, the acquisition of land, and the birth of a son;
when joined with gains of fortune and the like, it causes an increase in one's good luck. (59)
Through the grace of the Great King, the attainment of one's own desired goals brings happiness;
devotion to the gods and Brahmins brings about the acquisition of pearls and coral. (60)
When Venus is in the second, eleventh, or fifth house, or even in a trine or a quadrant, there is an increase in houses and fields, gain of wealth, and great happiness. (61)
If the lord of the eighth house is situated in the sixth, seventh, or eighth house from the lord of the second house, or is conjoined with malefic planets,
there will be suffering from living abroad, affliction by disease, death, and distress caused by thieves and the like.
If the lord of the second house is deficient [of strength], there will be fear of untimely death;
to remove that defect, one should cause the recitation of the Rudra-mantra to be performed.
One should give a white cow and silver; one attains the end [of suffering] without a doubt.
By the grace of Śaṅkara, there is no need for further deliberation on this matter. 64.

When the Sun has entered the sign of the Moon, and [the Moon] is in its exaltation or conjoined with its own domicile, and is situated in a quadrant, a trine, the eleventh house, the second house, or the third house; || 65 ||
There is the recovery of a lost kingdom and wealth, auspicious prosperity within the home, and the acquisition of villages, land, and other assets through the favor of friends and kings. (66)
The fruit of conception will be attained; Lakṣmī will cast her glance upon the home.
At the end of enjoyment, there will be physical lethargy and affliction by fever. (67)

If [the Moon] is situated in the eighth or the twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa, or is conjoined with malefic planets, there will be fear of kings, thieves, and snakes, as well as the occurrence of diseases such as fever. || 68 ||
If the lord of the second house is less than two [in strength], one undoubtedly suffers distress while traveling abroad; furthermore, there will be affliction from fever. (69)
To avoid those defects, one should perform the worship of Śiva;
thereafter, by the grace of Śaṅkara, one attains peace.
Now begins the chapter on the results of the major and minor periods (daśā-antardaśā) of Mars. 54.

O Brahmin, when Mars enters its own period, if it is situated in a quadrant (kendraka), a trine (trikoṇa), the eleventh house from the ascendant, or conjoined with a benefic, or if it is in the second house endowed with wealth, [the results are as follows]. || 1 ||
When [the Moon] is conjoined with the lord of the ascendant, there is the majesty of royal favor;
it brings about the signs of the glance of Fortune (Lakṣmī) and the recovery of lost kingdom and wealth. || 2 ||
There is joy from festivities for sons and other such events, and an abundance of cow's milk in the home,
when Mars is in its exaltation, its own sign, or its own division, and is endowed with strength.

There will be an increase in houses and fields, the acquisition of cattle, buffaloes, and other livestock, and through the favor of the great king, the fulfillment of one's desires shall bring happiness. (4)
Furthermore, if Mars is in the eighth or twelfth house, conjoined with or aspected by malefic planets,
there will be diseases such as urinary disorders and hemorrhoids, excessive suffering, and danger from wounds.
There will be affliction from thieves, snakes, and kings, as well as the depletion of wealth, grain, and cattle;
if the lord of the seventh house is in the second house, there is physical lethargy and mental anguish.
To avoid those defects, one should perform the recitation of the Rudra-mantra and give a bull as a gift for the removal of the defect caused by Mars.
By that, Bhauma becomes pleased through the grace of Śaṅkara;
he bestows health upon him and grants all prosperity. || 8 ||

When Rāhu enters the sub-period of Mars, and is situated in its exaltation or Mūlatrikoṇa, conjoined with benefics, aspected by benefics, and placed in a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine; || 9 ||

At that time, there will be honor from the king, the acquisition of houses, land, and so forth, as well as the gain of a wife and sons; through one's endeavors, the results will be even more abundant.
Likewise, when Rāhu is in the eighth or the twelfth house, conjoined with or aspected by a malefic, there is the attainment of the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā as well as travel to foreign lands.
There is fear of thieves, snakes, and wounds; the death of quadrupeds; fear of diseases caused by wind and bile (vāta-pitta); and confinement within a prison. || 12 ||
When Rāhu is situated in the second house, there is loss of wealth and great fear;
likewise, when he is in the seventh house, there is indeed great fear of untimely death.
One should perform the worship of the Nāga, feed the gods and Brahmins, and recite the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra for the sake of attaining long life and health. (14)

When Jupiter enters the sub-period of Mars, whether it is situated in a trine, a quadrant, the eleventh house, or the second house, or if it is in its exaltation degree or its own sign portion; || 15 ||
It brings good reputation, honor from the king, and the increase of wealth and grain;
it bestows auspicious prosperity in the home and the attainment of a wife, sons, and other blessings. || 16 ||

If [the lord of the year] is situated in a quadrant, a trine, or the eleventh house from the lord of the Dāya, or is conjoined with the lords of Bhāgya (the ninth) and Karma (the tenth), or joined with the lord of the Vāhana (the fourth house); || 17 ||

When [the Moon] is conjoined with the lord of the ascendant, situated in a benefic Navāṃśa, and placed in a benefic Varga, there is an increase in houses and fields, and auspicious prosperity within the home. (18)
There will be physical health, great fame, the acquisition of cattle, and the gain of four-footed animals; through one's enterprise, the results will be even more abundant.
There will be happiness from sons and wives, as well as the grandeur of royal honor,
when Jupiter is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, or when it is debilitated or set.
When [the Moon] is conjoined with or aspected by a malefic planet, or when it is weak,
there is fear of thieves, snakes, and kings, as well as the onset of bilious diseases and the like.

If the lord of the second house is weak, there will be affliction by spirits, the loss of servants, and the destruction of siblings; furthermore, there will be untimely death, fever, and the like. To ward off these evils, one should recite the Śivasahasraka.
When Saturn enters the sub-period of Mars, and [Mars] is situated in its own sign, or in a quadrant or a trine, or in a Mūlatrikoṇa, a quadrant, its exaltation degree, or its own Navāṃśa; || 23 ||
If Saturn is conjoined with or aspected by a benefic from the lord of the ascendant,
it brings royal happiness, increase in fame, and an abundance of grain in one's own village.
Accompanied by sons and grandsons, there shall be an accumulation of cattle and wealth in the home;
on its own day, it brings honor from the king, and in its own month, it causes the increase of progeny. (25)

When Saturn is situated in a base sign (nīca) or other such [debilitated] houses, or likewise in the eighth or twelfth house, there is fear from the rulers of barbarian tribes (mleccha), as well as the destruction of wealth, grain, and other assets.
If the lord of the second house is conjoined with malefic planets, there will be imprisonment in shackles, disease, and ultimately the destruction of one's fields; there will also be great fear.
In the Sanchara yoga, there is loss of wealth, enmity with the king, mental anguish,
affliction from thieves, fire, and the sovereign, as well as the destruction of one's uterine brothers.
Enmity with kinsmen, loss of life due to negligence, fear of sudden death, and suffering for one's children, wife, and others shall arise. (29)

There is fear of imprisonment and the like, as well as great terror from royal punishment, when the lord of the Mahādaśā is situated in a quadrant (kendrā), the eleventh house (lābha), or a trine (trikoṇa) from the lord of the Dāyā. || 30 ||
He obtains foreign travel as well as various kinds of ill repute;
he is constantly devoted to sinful deeds and is a killer of many living beings and so forth. || 31 ||
Sale of land, loss of fields, displacement from one's place, mental anguish, defeat in battle, and great fear arising from urinary disorders [shall occur]. (32)

If the lord of the Dāya is in the eighth or the twelfth house, or is conjoined with malefic planets, death should be known to occur during its period, along with affliction from kings, thieves, and the like. (33)
There will be affliction from wind, pain such as colic, and fear from kinsmen and enemies. || 34 ||
To avoid those faults, one should perform the recitation of the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra;
thereafter, one attains happiness through the grace of Śaṅkara.

When Mercury enters the sub-period of Mars and is situated in a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant, there will be excellent discourse, the giving of cows, a righteous intellect, and great fame. || 36 ||
Constant engagement in the path of policy, the eating of sweet food, vehicles, clothing, cattle, and other such things, as well as the duties of kingship—these are the pleasures [of this world]. (37)
Success in the fruits of agricultural work, as well as elephants, garments, and ornaments,
occurs even when [the lord] is in its sign of debilitation, set, or situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house.
Heart disease, loss of honor, imprisonment, destruction of kinsmen, the ruin of wife, sons, and wealth, and the loss of four-footed livestock shall occur. (39)
When conjoined with the lord of the period (daśādhipa), there is an increase in enemies, great fear, travel to foreign lands, and likewise various diseases. (40)
There will be opposition at the royal gate and even quarrels with one's own kinsmen;
however, if [the lord of the Dasa] is in a quadrant (kendra), a trine (trikoṇa), or its exaltation (svocca) from the lord of the Dasa, it brings about the acquisition of wealth. || 41 ||
It brings about the lordship over manifold wealth, as well as royal honor; it produces the yoga of a sovereign ruler, along with riches, garments, and ornaments. (42)
Earthly sounds such as drums and mṛdaṅgas, the position of a great commander, immense happiness, pure intellectual pastimes, garments, vehicles, and ornaments; || 43 ||

The wife, children, and other wealth in the house, as well as prosperity, are brought about by the side-glances [of the lord of the ascendant], provided that the lord of the Dasa is not situated in the sixth, twelfth, or eighth house from it, nor is he conjoined with malefic planets. (44)
In that period, there will be loss of honor, a cruel intellect, and harsh speech;
furthermore, there will be affliction from thieves, fire, and the king, as well as fear of bandits and the like on the road. (45)
There will undoubtedly be sudden quarrels when Mercury is liberated;
however, if its lord is in the second or the seventh house, there will be a terrifying great disease.
O Brahmin, one should perform the gift of a horse and the recitation of the thousand names of Viṣṇu; this bestows all prosperity and brings about the pacification of all misfortunes.
When Ketu enters the sub-period of Mars, whether it is situated in a trine, a quadrant, the second house, or the eleventh house, and is conjoined with or aspected by benefics; || 48 ||
There will be peace through the favor of the king, great happiness, and the arrival of wealth;
however, at the beginning of the period, there is some fruit, including the acquisition of land and the birth of a son. (49)

In the configuration where the lord of the tenth house is situated in the yoga-producing position and endowed with strength and vigor, there will be royal honors and the acquisition of four-footed living beings.

The attainment of a son, the increase of fame, the presence of prosperity in the home through her glance, the acquisition of wealth for one's circle of servants, the position of commander-in-chief, and great happiness. (51)

If [the lord of the eighth house] forms a friendship with the ruler of the earth (the Sun) and is adorned by sacrificial implements, garments, and so forth, yet is situated in the sixth or twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa and is conjoined with malefic planets; || 52 ||
Quarrels, dental diseases, affliction by thieves, tigers, and the like;
fever, dysentery, leprosy, and other ailments; and suffering for one's wife, children, and others. || 53 ||
In the second and seventh houses, there will be disease in the body,
humiliation, mental anguish, and the loss of wealth, grain, and other possessions.

When Venus enters the sub-period of Mars, and Venus is situated in a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine; or is in its own exaltation, or in its own sign, or is the lord of an auspicious house. || 55 ||

The acquisition of a kingdom, great happiness, elephants, horses, garments, and ornaments [result] from a connection with the lord of the ascendant; there is also the increase of children, wife, and so forth. (56)

There shall be an increase in lifespan, sovereignty, an increase in fortune, and happiness, if [the planet] is situated in a quadrant (kendram), a trine (koṇa), the eleventh house, or the second house from the lord of the period (dāyeśa). (57)
At that time, one attains prosperity, the birth of a son, and great happiness;
it brings great joy from one's own master and results in the acquisition of wealth, clothing, and other such things. || 58 ||
Through the favor of the great king, it bestows the acquisition of villages, land, and so forth;
at the end of its enjoyment, one obtains the fruit consisting of the attainment of song, dance, and other such pleasures.
When he is endowed with the presiding power of his past actions, he will obtain the merit of bathing at sacred fords and cause wells,
ponds, and tanks to be constructed as reservoirs of meritorious dharma and compassion.

If [the Moon] is situated in the eighth or twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa, or in the sixth house conjoined with malefic planets, it causes an abundance of suffering, bodily affliction, and loss of wealth. (61)
It causes fear of kings, thieves, and the like, as well as domestic quarrels, suffering for one's wife and children, and the destruction of cattle, buffaloes, and other livestock. (62)
If the lord of the second house is less than two [years old], there will be affliction of the body;
one should give a white cow or a buffalo for the increase of longevity and health. (63)

When the Sun enters the sub-period of Mars, and the Sun is situated in its exaltation, its own sign, a quadrant, a Mūlatrikoṇa, or the eleventh house, or is conjoined with the lords of the ninth or tenth houses; || 64 ||
By eating that [food], one obtains a vehicle, fame, and the birth of a son;
there shall be an abundance of wealth and grain in the home, along with auspicious prosperity. (65)
Security, health, great fortitude, honor from the king, and great happiness; through perseverance, an abundance of results and an audience with the king in a foreign land. (66)
If the lord of the Dāya (year) is in the sixth, eighth, twelfth, or associated with malefic planets,
there will be physical suffering, mental anguish, loss of undertakings, and great fear.
If the lord of the second house is in the eighth house, there will be diseases of the head, fever and the like, or even dysentery; furthermore, there is danger from snakes, fever, and poison.
One should perform the propitiatory rite according to the prescribed rules to pacify the fear of suffering from diseases;
it brings about physical health as well as an accumulation of wealth and grain. (69)

When the Moon enters the sub-period of Mars, and that Moon is in its exaltation, its own sign, or a quadrant, and is joined with the lord of the seventh house, the lord of the vehicle (the fourth house), the lord of the tenth house, or the lord of the ascendant; || 70 ||
He exercises extensive sovereignty, [providing] perfumes, garlands, garments, and the like; he constructs tanks, city gates, and so forth, and accumulates merit, dharma, and other virtues. (71)
It brings about the performance of marriage and festive rites, bestows happiness through wife, children, and so forth,
grants the attainment of joy for one's father and mother, and causes the Goddess of Fortune to cast her favorable glances upon the home.
Through the grace of the Great King, one obtains the happiness of accomplishing one's own desires and so forth;
when the moon is full, the fruit is complete, but when it is waning, the fruit becomes small. (73)

If [the planet] is situated in a debilitation sign, in the eighth or sixth house from the lord of the Dasa, or in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from it, there will be death or suffering for wife and children, as well as the destruction of land. (74)
There will be the depletion of livestock and grain, as well as fear caused by thieves and the like;
moreover, if the lord of the second house is deficient, untimely death (apamṛtyu) will occur.
One should perform the recitation of the Durgā-Lakṣmī mantra for stiffness of the body and mental distress;
one should give a white cow or a buffalo as a gift, and this shall ordain freedom from disease.
Now begins the chapter on the results of the sub-periods within the periods (Rahvantardaśā). || 55 ||
If Rāhu is in Cancer, Scorpio, Virgo, or Sagittarius,
and is transiting that sign, one receives royal honor, as well as clothing, vehicles, and ornaments.
Through perseverance, there is an abundance of results; it brings gain from four-footed creatures and life-sustenance.
In the western portion, it brings travel and the acquisition of vehicles and garments.

If Rāhu is in an upacaya house from the ascendant, conjoined with or aspected by a benefic planet, situated in a friendly navāṃśa or a sign of exaltation, and associated with a yoga-kāraka, [the yoga is formed]. (3)
It brings about the acquisition of a kingdom, great energy, the favor of kings, and auspiciousness; it produces the wealth of happiness and the increase of wife, sons, and other kin. || 4 ||

O twice-born one, if Rāhu is in the eighth or the twelfth house from the ascendant, conjoined with or aspected by malefic planets, there will be suffering from wounds caused by thieves and the like; such results occur everywhere in this manner.
Hatred from the people at the royal gate, the destruction of beloved kinsmen, and suffering for one's wife, children, and others will certainly occur; of this there is no doubt. (6)

If the lord of the second house is in the seventh house, or if [the lord] occupies the seventh house, there will always be disease and great suffering; one should perform propitiatory rites according to the prescribed rules,
O twice-born one, and then health and prosperity will surely come to pass.
When Jupiter has entered Rāhu (is eclipsed) and is situated in a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant, or is in its exaltation, its own sign, or even in its exaltation or own-sign Navāṃśa; || 8 ||
One attains a favorable position, mental fortitude, the destruction of enemies, great happiness, royal favor, and supreme well-being. (9)
Day by day there is growth, like the moon in the bright fortnight;
there will be abundant wealth such as vehicles and the like, and the house will be crowded with cattle. (10)
In the southwest and the western quarter, there will be a journey and an audience with the king;
there shall be success in one's duties and purposes, and one will return once more to one's own country. (11)
Service rendered to Brahmins, undertaking pilgrimages and similar rites, the acquisition of vehicles and villages, and the worship of gods and Brahmins—[these are the fruits]. (12)
There is constant joy from festivals for one's sons and the like, as well as the eating of sweet foods,
even when [the Moon] is in a debilitated sign, set, or situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house.
If [the Moon] is joined with a malefic in the enemy's sign, there will be loss of wealth;
he will encounter obstacles in his undertakings, and a loss of honor will arise. || 14 ||
There will be suffering caused by wife and children, as well as heart disease brought about by the king,
if [the Moon] is in a quadrant, a trine, the eleventh house, or the second house from the lord of the Dasa.
In Duścikya, which is full of strength, there is the increase of houses, fields, and so forth;
as well as the giving of food, clothing, cattle, and the like, along with dharma, recitation, and other such acts. (16)

At the end of the period of enjoyment, due to the king's wrath, there will be physical suffering for two months, as well as the destruction of the elder brother and affliction to the mother, father, and others. (17)

If the lord of the Dasa is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from the Lagna, or is conjoined with malefic planets, there will be loss of wealth during that period and physical suffering will occur. || 18 ||
If the lord of the second house is less than two [years old], untimely death will occur;
therefore, the offering of a golden image and the worship of Śiva should be performed.
O best of the twice-born, by the grace of Śrī Śambhu, the planet becomes pleased;
it bestows health upon the body and brings peace to the wise man.

When Saturn enters the sub-period of Rāhu and is situated in a quadrant (kendraka), a trine (trikoṇa) from the ascendant, or in its own exaltation, its Mūlatrikoṇa, or in the sign of Dvīcika (Capricorn) or the eleventh house; || 21 ||
During its consumption, service to the king is auspicious and pleasing to the monarch;
likewise, performing marriages, festivals, and meritorious deeds in abundance [is beneficial]. (22)
One intent on establishing a grove shall have a tank constructed;
through the power of a Śūdra master, there will be the attainment of desired objects and the accumulation of cattle-wealth. || 23 ||
In the western part, there is a journey from the presence of the Lord, followed by the loss of wealth;
there will be physical lethargy and meager results, yet one shall return to one's own country.
If Saturn is situated in its sign of debilitation, in an inimical sign, or in the eighth or twelfth house,
there will be fear of enemies and kings, as well as suffering for one's wife, children, and others.
One will incur mental anguish for oneself and one's kinsmen, disputes with heirs, and sudden quarrels in legal proceedings; yet, one may also obtain ornaments. || 26 ||
If the lord of the Dasa is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, or is conjoined with malefic planets, there will be heart disease, loss of honor, disputes, and suffering from enemies. (27)
Wandering to other lands and such places will cause one to suffer from diseases like a thicket;
there will be bad food such as *kodrava* and fear arising from the suffering of one's caste. (28)
If the lord of the second house is deficient [in strength], untimely death will occur;
one should give a black cow or a buffalo as a gift, and through this donation, one may predict recovery from illness.

When Mercury enters the sub-period of Rahu, or when it is situated in the ninth house, or even in its own sign, or in its exaltation, or in a quadrant, or when Jupiter is endowed with strength; || 30 ||
It brings about a royal yoga within the home that increases prosperity, the acquisition of wealth through business, and the attainment of excellent knowledge and vehicles. (31)
Marriage ceremonies and festive activities bring the acquisition of four-footed animals;
in the month of Saumya (Mārgaśīrṣa), there is great happiness, and on its own day, an audience with the king.
There will be fragrant flowers, beds, and the like, as well as exceedingly beautiful female companionship;
through the favor of a great king, there shall be the acquisition of wealth and great fame. (33)

If [the lord of the year] is in a quadrant, the eleventh house, or the third house from the lord of the year, or if it is in the ninth or tenth house, there will be bodily health, enthusiasm of heart, and the attainment of desired goals, bringing happiness. (34)

The fame of those of meritorious renown and the like, the listening to Purāṇas and so forth, marriage, initiation for sacrifice, and the practice of charity, righteousness, compassion, and the rest. (35)
If Mercury is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, conjoined with or aspected by Saturn;
or if it is in the sixth, twelfth, or eighth house from the lord of the Mahādaśā, conjoined with malefic planets; || 36 ||
He who reviles gods and Brahmins will be deprived of enjoyments and fortune;
being devoid of truth and possessed of a wicked intellect, he shall suffer affliction from thieves, snakes, and kings. (37)
There will be sudden quarrels, the loss of one's teacher, sons, and so forth, expenditure of wealth, royal displeasure, and suffering for one's wife, children, and others. (38)
Or, if the lord of the second house is deficient [in strength], one should predict the fear of untimely death;
for the sake of averting that affliction, one should recite the *Viṣṇusahasranāma* one thousand times.
When Ketu enters the sub-period of Rāhu, there is wandering about, fear of the king,
diseases such as wind-fever (vātajvara) and others, and loss of four-footed livestock.
If the eighth house is conjoined with malefic planets, there will be physical lethargy and mental anguish;

however, if it is conjoined with or aspected by benefics, there will be bodily comfort, the arrival of wealth, the attainment of honor and ornaments from the king, and it will bring auspiciousness to the home. || 41 ||
When there is a connection with the lord of the ascendant, the accomplishment of desired goals brings happiness;
or, when [the planet] is conjoined with the lord of the ascendant, gain certainly occurs. (42)

There will be the acquisition of four-footed animals if Ketu is situated in a quadrant (kendraka) or a trine (trikoṇa); or if Ketu is situated in the eighth house or the twelfth house, being devoid of strength. || 43 ||
During its period, there will be many diseases, suffering from thieves, snakes, and wounds;
separation from father and mother, hatred toward brothers, and mental anguish. (44)
If the lord of the second house is less than two [years old], there will be affliction of the body;
to ward off that evil, one should cause the gift of medicine to be made. || 45 ||

When Venus enters the sub-period of Rāhu and is situated in a quadrant, a trine, or the eleventh house from the Karakamsha, endowed with strength, one should predict the full potency of the yoga. || 46 ||
From a Brahmin one obtains wealth, which brings the gain of cows, buffaloes, and the like;
there is joy through the birth of a son and other festivities, and auspicious events occur within the home. (47)
Honor, royal recognition, the attainment of a kingdom, and great happiness [result] when [a planet] is in its exaltation, its own sign, its exaltation degree, or its own degree. || 48 ||
The construction of a new house, the constant eating of sweet foods, the prosperity of wife and sons, association with friends, and excellent meals [are obtained]. (49)
The gift of food is always dear, as is the practice of charity, righteousness, and other such virtues;
through the favor of the great king, one obtains vehicles, garments, and ornaments.

From perseverance comes an abundance of results; yet marriage and the tying of the sacred thread [are unfavorable] when Venus is situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, or is debilitated or in the house of an enemy. (51)
When conjoined with Mandāra-phaṇi, one should predict disease during its period;
it also causes sudden quarrels and brings about separation between father and son. (52)
There will be loss of one's own kinsmen, suffering for people everywhere, and quarrels with heirs, which will bring about the death of oneself and one's master. (53)

There will be suffering for wife and children, and the occurrence of diseases such as colic (śūla), when [the planet] is situated in a quadrant (kendrā) or a trine (trikoṇa) from the lord of the period (dāyeśa). || 54 ||

Or, if the eleventh house is occupied by the lord of the tenth house, there will be great happiness from the local guardian deity, as well as the pleasure of fragrant garments, beds, and so forth, along with the enjoyment of singing and instrumental music. || 55 ||

The acquisition of ornaments such as chowries and whisks, along with beloved objects, occurs when the lord of the Dasha is situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from the Moon, or is conjoined with malefic planets. || 56 ||
From passing urine while facing a Brahmin, a king, or a thief, there arises great fear;
from urinary disorder (prameha), a blood-related disease occurs; and from eating contemptible food, there is headache. (57)
There will be entry into prison and loss of wealth due to royal punishment;
or, if the lord of the second house is weak, there will be the destruction of wife, children, and so forth.
There will indeed be affliction to oneself, fear, and even the fear of untimely death;
one should perform the recitation of the Durgā-lakṣmī mantra, and thereafter one shall obtain happiness. || 59 ||
When the Sun enters the Antardasha of Rahu, and is situated in its exaltation, its own sign, a quadrant, a trine, the eleventh house, or in its exaltation degree or its own Navamsha degree; || 60 ||
When aspected by a benefic planet, it brings auspiciousness that delights the king,
as well as abundance of wealth and grain, and conveys happiness through modesty.
There will be lordship over a small village and very little gain, even when [the Moon] is conjoined with the lord of the ninth house or aspected by the lord of the tenth house. || 62 ||
Resorting to a king, great fame, as well as traveling to foreign lands, the attainment of sovereignty over a country, and elephants, horses, garments, and ornaments. (63)

If the lord of the ninth house (the house of mercy) is situated in the twelfth, the eleventh, the eighth, the sixth, or even in its sign of debilitation, it bestows the fulfillment of one's heart's desires and the birth of virtuous sons.
There will be fever and dysentery, quarrels, conflict with the king, departure [from home], increase of enemies, and affliction from kings, thieves, and fire. (65)
If [the lord of the year] is in a quadrant, a trine, the tenth house, or the eleventh house from the lord of the Dasa,
there will be honor from the king in a foreign land, as well as auspiciousness and welfare.
If the lord of the second house is less than two [years old], there will be a serious illness;
one should perform prostrations to the Sun and rites for peace to bring about health.

When the Moon is within the period of Rāhu, even if it is in its own sign or its exaltation, or in a quadrant, a trine, or the eleventh house, or in the sign of a friend, conjoined with a benefic; || 68 ||
Sovereignty, honor from kings, the acquisition of wealth for the sake of riches, health, ornaments, and the prosperity of friends, wives, and sons. (69)

When the moon is full, the result is complete; through the favor of the king, it brings auspiciousness, the acquisition of horses and vehicles, and causes the increase of houses, fields, and other assets. (70)

If the lord of the eighth house is situated in the fourth, the ninth, a quadrant, or the eleventh house from it, there will be signs of fortune’s favor and the occurrence of auspiciousness in the home. (71)
There shall be the accomplishment of all undertakings, bringing wealth, grain, and happiness;
one should perform the propitiation of the Goddess for the sake of attaining good fame and honor. (72)

If the lord of the eighth house (dāyeśa) is situated in the sixth, the eighth, or the twelfth house and is devoid of strength, there will be loss of house, land, and wealth due to ghosts, petty thieves, tigers, and the like. (73)
On the path there is fear of thieves, excessive wounds, and great calamity;
when the lord of the second house is deficient [in strength], then untimely death shall occur. (74)
One should give a white cow or a female buffalo to a Brahmin for the attainment of health;
thereafter, one obtains happiness through the grace of the moon during its eclipse.

When Mars enters the sub-period of Rāhu, if it is situated in the eleventh house, a trine from the ascendant, or in a quadrant, conjoined with a benefic, or even in its own exaltation or its own sign; || 76 ||
Through the grace of one's chosen deity, one shall regain a lost kingdom and wealth, effect the increase of house and fields, and become a partaker of the happiness of progeny. || 77 ||

There is great happiness from food obtained quickly, and the acquisition of ornaments, horses, garments, and so forth, when [the Moon] is in a quadrant (kendra), a trine (koṇa), the second house, the eleventh house, or the tenth house from the lord of the period (dāyeśa). || 78 ||
There will be the acquisition of red garments and the like, a journey, an audience with a king, auspiciousness among one's circle of sons, and great happiness from one's own lord. (79)
There will be the position of commander-in-chief, great enthusiasm, and the acquisition of wealth from one's circle of brothers,
if the lord of the ninth house is situated in the eighth, twelfth, or sixth house, or is conjoined with malefic planets.
There shall be loss of children, wife, and so forth, as well as affliction for servants;
there will be displacement from one's position and conflict with kinsmen, wives, and sons. (81)
There will be fear of thieves, snakes, and wounds, as well as affliction of one's own body; it causes distress at the beginning, but one shall obtain happiness in the middle and at the end. (82)
If the lord of the second house is less than two [signs] away [from its exaltation], there will be great physical lethargy and great fear;
one should give an ox and a cow for the sake of obtaining health and happiness. 83.
Now begins the chapter on the results of the sub-periods (antardaśā) of Jupiter. 56.

When Jupiter is in its exaltation or its own sign, and is situated in a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant, the native becomes either the lord of many kings or a prosperous person honored by the king. || 1 ||
There will be the acquisition of female buffaloes and the like, as well as clothing, vehicles, and ornaments; and the construction of a new residence provided with mansions and walls. (2)
The attainment of sovereignty over elephants, the emergence of the fruits of fortune and karma, the honor bestowed by Brahmins and masters, and the equal vision of the Lord. (3)

It bestows the excellence of its own results for its lord and brings the acquisition of a wife, sons, and so forth; however, if situated in its sign of debilitation, in a degree of debilitation, or in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, [it causes the opposite].

Association with the base brings great suffering, as does conflict with one's kinsmen; for such a person there is quarreling and no reflection, leading even to untimely death at the hands of his own masters.
There will be separation from children and wife, as well as loss of wealth, grain, and property; due to the affliction of the lord of the seventh house, there will be divine oppression.
To avoid those defects, one should recite the *Śivasahasraka*;
and for the attainment of one's desired goal, one should perform the *Rudrajāpya* and the gift of a cow (*godāna*).

When Saturn is within the sub-period of Jupiter, situated in its exaltation, its own sign, or the sign of a friend, placed in a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant, or in the eleventh house endowed with strength; || 8 ||
The acquisition of a kingdom brings great happiness, accompanied by garments and ornaments;
there is also the gain of wealth, grain, and other riches, as well as the gain of a wife, which produces much joy.

It brings the acquisition of vehicles, clothing, cattle, and land; it grants the attainment of a position and provides happiness through sons, friends, and others, as well as the fortune of riding upon men.
He obtains blue garments and the like, and he acquires a blue horse;
there is a journey toward the western direction and an audience with the king.
One should predict the acquisition of various vehicles during periods of slow income when Saturn is in the sixth,
eighth, or twelfth house from the ascendant, or is debilitated or heliacally set, while Mars is likewise situated [in those same houses].
There will be the loss of wealth, grain, and other possessions; suffering from fever, mental anguish, affliction for wife and children, or the arising of pain from wounds and the like. (13)
In the home, however, there will be inauspicious activities, suffering for the circle of servants and others, loss of cattle, buffaloes, and so forth, and he will become a hater of his kinsmen. (14)

If [the lord of the ninth house] is situated in a quadrant (kendraka), a trine (koṇa), the eleventh house, or even the second house from the lord of the year, there will be gain of land, gain of wealth, and the happiness of obtaining a son. || 15 ||

There will be the acquisition of cows, buffaloes, and the like, as well as wealth from the source of Śūdras, when the lord of the Dāya (the ninth house) is situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, or is conjoined with malefic planets. || 16 ||
There will be the loss of wealth, grain, and so forth, as well as causing discord with kinsmen and friends;
there will be the failure of one's endeavors, bodily affliction, and great fear from one's own people. (17)
If Saturn is the lord of the second or seventh house, untimely death will surely occur;
to ward off that evil, one should recite the Viṣṇusahasranāma.
One should give a black cow as a buffalo; by this, one may predict health. Through the grace of the slow-moving planet [Saturn], O best of the twice-born, this is the truth, the absolute truth. (19)

When a benefic planet is situated within the Antardasha of the Jeeva (Jupiter), occupying a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine; or when it is in its exaltation, its own sign, or conjoined with the lord of the Mahadasha. || 20 ||
There shall be gain of wealth and physical well-being, the attainment of a kingdom and great happiness;
through the favor of the Great King, the fulfillment of one's desires shall bring forth bliss. (21)
When the house is seen by the son of the Earth (Mars), it is crowded with vehicles, clothing, cattle, and other wealth; yet there is an increase of enemies and a loss of happiness.

From exertion, the result is the attainment of fruit, though there may be suffering from fever and indigestion; this occurs when the lord of the Mahādaśā is in the ninth or fifth house, or in a quadrant, occupying its own exaltation sign. (23)
There will be gain of wealth in one's own country, bringing happiness to father and mother;
and, through the favor of royal friends, one will be endowed with elephants and horses.

If the lord of the eighth house is situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from the lord of the Mahadasha, or is conjoined with malefic planets and devoid of the aspect of benefics, there will be the loss of grain and wealth. || 25 ||
Traveling abroad, fear of thieves on the road, afflictions such as wounds, burning sensations, and eye diseases, and wandering through various lands. (26)
If the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from the ascendant is conjoined with malefic planets,
there will be constant quarrels and harshness within the home.
There will be loss of four-footed livestock and likewise in business dealings;
furthermore, there will be fear of untimely death and conflict with enemies. (28)
If [the lord of the ascendant] is aspected by benefics and joined with benefics, there is happiness from a spouse and the arrival of wealth;
in the beginning, there is auspiciousness, physical comfort, and the acquisition of vehicles and clothing. (29)
If there is loss of wealth at the beginning [of the year], happiness for one's own self will not arise;
or, if the lord of the second house is weak, premature death will occur.
To avoid those defects, one should recite the Viṣṇusahasraka;
it increases longevity and bestows all forms of prosperity.
When Ketu is within the Antardasha of Jupiter and is conjoined with a benefic planet,
there is a limited acquisition of happiness and wealth, and the consumption of inferior food.

If the lord of the ninth house (dāyeśa) is situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from the ascendant and is conjoined with malefic planets, one will obtain food from others, food from funeral rites (śrāddha),
and wealth from sources rooted in sin.
Royal wrath, loss of wealth, imprisonment, affliction by disease, loss of strength, hatred toward one's father, hatred toward one's brothers, and mental anguish. (34)
If the lord of the ninth house is situated in the fifth, the ninth, the fourth, or the tenth house,
there is the yoga of a human vehicle (naravāhana), and one will be surrounded by elephants, horses, and garments.

Through the favor of the great king, it brings about the attainment of one's desired goals and purposes; through industrious effort, it yields abundant results and the acquisition of cattle, buffaloes, and other such wealth. (36)
If the lord of the second house is in the sub-period of the lord of the seventh house, it brings the acquisition of wealth, clothing, and so forth;
however, if the lord of the second house is in the sub-period of the lord of the seventh house, there will be affliction to the body.
One should perform the gift of liberality, practice the recitation of the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra,
and carry out the propitiatory rite that pacifies all defects according to the prescribed injunctions.

When Venus is within the Antardasha of Jupiter, conjoined with the lord of the ninth house or the tenth house, or situated in the eleventh or fifth house, in its own sign, or conjoined with a benefic; || 39 ||

There will be the mounting of men as vehicles, accompanied by elephants, horses, and garments; through the favor of a great king, there will be an abundance of gains and great happiness, and there will also be the acquisition of blue and red garments. (40)
O best of Brahmins, a journey toward the eastern direction brings the acquisition of wealth, auspiciousness, great joy, and happiness for one's father and mother. (41)
Devotion to the deities and the guru, as well as the great gift of food, and the construction of tanks, city gates, and so forth—let him bestow such merits in abundance. (42)

If the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house is in its sign of debilitation, or likewise from the lord of the Dasa, there will be strife, discord with kinsmen, and suffering for one's wife, children, and others. (43)
When Mandāra is conjoined with Rāhu, there is quarrel and fear from the king;
likewise, there is quarrel on account of women and quarrel with one's father-in-law.
There will be a dispute with a brother and a loss of wealth and grain if [the planet] is situated in a quadrant from the lord of the Dasa, or in the second or ninth house. (45)
There will be the acquisition of wealth, grain, and so forth, as well as the gain of a wife and an audience with the king. || 46 ||
There will be vehicles, the birth of a son, an increase in livestock, great happiness, devotion to singing and instrumental music, and association with learned people. || 47 ||

When Venus is the lord of the seventh or twelfth house, there is the enjoyment of divine food and happiness from nourishing one's own kinsmen; however, during its periods (daśās), there is loss of wealth. (48)
He faces the danger of untimely death arising from women, roots, medicinal herbs, and the like;
for the pacification of that disease, one should perform rites of propitiation (śāntikarma). || 49 ||
One should give a white cow or a buffalo for the increase of longevity and health;
through the propitiation of the planet Venus, one shall thereafter attain happiness. (50)
When the Sun is within the Antardasha of Jupiter, or when it is in its exaltation, its own sign, a quadrant, a trine, the twelfth house, or the eleventh house; || 51 ||
Or, if [the lord of the ascendant] is joined with wealth or strength, or likewise from the lord of the period (dāyeśa),
there will be gain of wealth at that time, as well as the splendor of royal honor.
The acquisition of vehicles, clothing, cattle, and ornaments, the birth of a son, and the subjugation of friends and lords—these are desired and bring auspiciousness in all undertakings. (53)
If the Sun is in the eighth or twelfth house from the ascendant, or likewise from the lord of the Dasa,
there will be suffering from diseases of the head and the like, as well as suffering from fever.
At that time, he becomes deficient in virtuous deeds and likewise accumulates a mass of evil karma;
indeed, he incurs the hatred of all people and suffers separation from his kinsmen. (55)
If the Sun is in the Antardasha of Jupiter, there will be sudden quarrels;
however, if the lord of the second house is also the lord of the seventh house, bodily affliction will occur.
To avoid those defects, one should recite the Ādityahṛdaya;
through the grace of the glorious Sūrya, all afflictions are pacified. (57)
When the Moon is within the Antardasha of Jupiter, and is situated in a quadrant, the eleventh house, a trine, its own exaltation, or its own sign, and is full and endowed with strength; || 58 ||
If [the Moon] is situated in the sixth house from the lord of the Dasa, there will be honor and prosperity from the king,
as well as happiness from wife, children, and the like, and likewise the enjoyment of milk-based foods.
Likewise, virtuous deeds and fame shall bring about the increase of sons, grandsons, and so forth;
through the favor of the great king, there shall be all happiness and the arrival of wealth. (60)

There is happiness for many people and the accumulation of merit through acts such as giving when the Moon is situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, or is conjoined with malefic planets. (61)
If the lord of the Dasa is devoid of strength and situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house,
there will be loss of honor, wealth, and kinsmen, as well as exile to a foreign land.
There will be affliction from kings, thieves, and the like, as well as conflict with kinsmen, separation from maternal uncles and others, and likewise suffering for one's mother. (63)
If [the planet] is in the second or the sixth house from the lord [of the year], there will be affliction of the body;
to ward off that evil, one should cause the recitation of the Durgā-pāṭha to be performed.

When Mars is within the Antardasha of Jupiter, and is situated in a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant, or in its own exaltation, or in its own sign, or in its exaltation degree, or even in its own Navamsha degree; || 65 ||
It brings about the acquisition of knowledge, marriage, and undertakings, as well as the gain of villages, land, and so forth;
it attains the power of the people and grants the fulfillment of all objectives and purposes. 66.
If the lord of the second house is situated in a quadrant (kendraka), a trine (koṇa), the eleventh house, or the second house,
and is joined with or aspected by benefics, there will be abundance of wealth, grain, and other riches.
The abundance of giving sweet foods brings auspiciousness that delights the king;
likewise, there is the happiness of women, the attainment of sons, and the fruit of visiting holy pilgrimage sites.
If the lord of the eighth house from the lord of the Mahadasha is situated in the eighth or the twelfth house, or is in its sign of debilitation,
or is conjoined with or aspected by malefic planets, there will be the destruction of grain, wealth, and home.
There is no fear of various diseases nor the occurrence of ailments such as eye disorders;
there is greater hardship in the first half [of life] and great happiness in the second half. (70)
If the lord of the second house is less than two signs away [from the Moon], there will be physical lethargy and mental distress;
however, the gift of a bull bestows all prosperity.
When Rāhu is within the Antardasha of Jupiter, or when it is in its exaltation, or in a quadrant, or in its Mūlatrikoṇa, or in the ninth house, and is joined with the lord of a quadrant; || 72 ||
If [the Moon] is conjoined with or aspected by a benefic, one should predict union and pleasure;
during the period of enjoyment and so forth, for five months, one shall obtain wealth, grain, and other such things. (73)
There will be a visit from a Yavana lord to one's district or village;
there will be an abundance of auspiciousness in the home and the command of a large army.

Traveling on long journeys and the like, the accumulation of merit, virtue, and so forth, the attainment of the fruits of bathing at sacred fords, and the accomplishment of desired goals—all these bring about happiness. (75)
