If the eighth or twelfth house from the Dāya [ascendant] is conjoined with malefic planets, there will be fear of thieves, snakes, and wounds, as well as adversity from the king. || 76 ||
He will certainly become distressed by a multitude of household duties;
there will be discord with his uterine brother and conflict with his kinsmen. (77)
In the house, however, inauspicious events will certainly occur, along with the fear of bad dreams and the like;
there will be sudden quarrels, and diseases such as smallpox and consumption will arise.
When Rāhu is situated in the second or seventh house, one should predict bodily affliction;
to remedy that defect, one should perform the recitation of the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra.
O best of the twice-born, by performing the gift of charity, one shall obtain all happiness through the grace of the worship of the gods and the satisfaction of Rāhu.
Now begins the chapter on the results of the sub-periods (antardaśā) of Saturn. 57.

If [the Moon] is in its Mūlatrikoṇa or its own sign, or in Libra (Tulā), or even in its exaltation, or in a quadrant, a trikoṇa, or the eleventh house, or endowed with Rājayoga and other such configurations; || 1 ||
The attainment of a kingdom, great happiness, the increase of wife, sons, and so forth, along with a multitude of three types of vehicles—elephants, horses, and garments. (2)
Through the favor of the great king, it brings the attainment of the rank of commander-in-chief and other honors;
it results in the acquisition of four-footed creatures and the gain of villages, lands, and so forth. (3)

Likewise, if Saturn is in the eighth or twelfth house, or is debilitated or conjoined with malefic planets, there will be fear of the king and suffering from poison, weapons, and the like at the commencement of its period and sub-periods.

There will be discharge of blood, diseases such as abdominal tumors (gulma), suffering from dysentery and similar ailments, fear of thieves and other dangers in the middle of one's life, exile from one's country, and mental anguish.
O twice-born one, the sub-period (antardaśā) of Śani at the end [of the main period] brings about auspiciousness;
however, if the lord of the second or the seventh house is [involved], untimely death (apamṛtyu) will occur.
To avoid those faults, one should perform the recitation of the Mrtyuñjaya mantra;
thereafter, one attains peace through the grace of Śaṅkara.
When Mercury enters the sign of the Moon, or occupies a trine or a quadrant,
there is honor, fame, renown, acquisition of learning, and the arrival of wealth.

One attains happiness in one's own country, endowed with the fruits of vehicles and other such things, as well as the successful accomplishment of rites such as sacrifices and the arising of royal yoga and the like. || 9 ||
There is physical comfort, enthusiasm in the heart, and the occurrence of auspiciousness in the home;
the fruit of bathing at the Setu is obtained through such acts as pilgrimage to sacred fords.
There shall be gain of wealth through trade, the hearing of the Purāṇas and so forth, the fruit of giving food, and the constant eating of sweet foods. (11)
When Mercury is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, or is debilitated or set,
and is conjoined with the Sun, Mars, or Rahu— or likewise from the lord of the Dasa— [the results are unfavorable].

The results at the beginning are such as the coronation of a king, the attainment of wealth, and lordship over a country or village; however, in the middle and at the end, there is the affliction of disease.
All undertakings will perish, there will be agitation and great fear;
if the second or seventh house is afflicted, there will be physical suffering. (14)
To avoid those faults, one should recite the Viṣṇusahasraka and perform the gift of food, which bestows all prosperity. || 15 ||
When Ketu is within the period of Saturn, being aspected by or conjoined with benefics, or situated in its own exaltation, in a benefic sign, or conjoined with a Yoga-kāraka; || 16 ||
If [a planet] is situated in the center or at an angle, there is displacement from one's position and great fear;
there is poverty, imprisonment, terror, and the destruction of children, wife, and so forth. (17)

If [the Moon] is conjoined with the lord of the ascendant, there will be great hardship for one's own master as well as travel to a foreign land; however, at the outset, there will be happiness and the arrival of wealth.

Bathing at all sacred fords such as the Gaṅgā and beholding the deities [occur] when [the lord of the ninth house] is in a quadrant, a trine, or in the sign of the third house from the lord of the ninth.
One becomes capable, possesses a mind devoted to righteousness, attains happiness, and meets with kings;
likewise, this occurs when Ketu is in the eighth or the twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa.
There is indeed fear of untimely death, the eating of contemptible food, cold fever and diarrhea, and affliction from wounds, thieves, and the like. (21)
Separation from wife and children occurs inevitably in this worldly existence;
if [the Moon] is situated in the second or the seventh house, there will be affliction of the body. (22)
One should indeed perform the gift of charity, which wards off untimely death;
through the propitiation of the planet Ketu, one shall attain happiness and peace. || 23 ||
When Venus is within the period of Saturn, whether situated in its exaltation, its own sign, or in a quadrant, conjoined with a benefic, or in a trine or the eleventh house; || 24 ||
The acquisition of a wife, sons, and wealth; bodily health; great festivals;
the attainment of auspicious prosperity within the home; the gain of a kingdom; and great happiness. (25)

Through the favor of the great king, there is the attainment of desired goals bringing happiness, as well as honor, the respect of one's master, and the acquisition of dear garments and other such things. (26)
From another continent, there is the acquisition of clothing, as well as a white horse and a buffalo;
through the influence of Jupiter’s movement, there is good fortune, happiness, and abundance of wealth.
Due to the movement of Saturn, this man undoubtedly attains yoga when Venus is in its enemy sign,
its sign of debilitation, or in its setting, or situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house.
The loss of a wife brings mental affliction; the loss of one's position brings mental anguish;
the suffering of one's own kin through the loss of wives brings distress; and conflict with people brings torment. (29)

If [the lord of the year] is in the ninth house from the lord of the year, or in a quadrant (kendram), or conjoined with the eleventh house, it brings favor from the king and grants one's heart's desires. || 30 ||
The fruit of being endowed with the practice of charity, righteousness, and compassion, such as pilgrimages to sacred fords and the like;
the composition of poetry whose meaning is based on the scriptures; and the hearing of the Vedānta and so forth. (31)
One obtains happiness from wife, children, and so forth; there is no doubt about this.
[This occurs] when Venus is in the twelfth, sixth, or even the eighth house from the lord of the Dasa.
There is pain in the eyes, fear of fever, and abandonment of one's own family customs; there is toothache and the like in the cheeks, and affliction in the heart and the private parts. (33)
Fear of water, mental anguish arising from the possibility of falling from a tree, hostility toward people at the king's gate, and conflict with one's own brother. (34)
If the lord of the second or the seventh house is [malefic], there will be suffering for oneself;
to avoid that fault, one should perform the recitation (japa) of the goddess Durgā.
One should give a white cow or a buffalo, which bestows the increase of longevity and health;
through the grace of Jagadambā, one shall thereafter attain happiness. || 36 ||

When the Sun is within the sign of Mars, or even when it is in its exaltation or its own house, and is conjoined with the lord of the ninth house (bhāgya) or situated in a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine; || 37 ||
Or even when joined with a benefic aspect, there is great happiness from one's own master;
in the home, there is the attainment of auspicious prosperity and an increase in the happiness of sons and others. || 38 ||
The house will be crowded with vehicles, clothing, livestock, and the like, as well as cow's milk,
when the Sun is in the eighth or twelfth house from the Ascendant, or likewise from the lord of the Dasa.
Heart disease, loss of honor, displacement from one's position, mental anguish, separation from beloved kinsmen, and the destruction of one's endeavors. (40)
Furthermore, there is suffering from heat, fever, and the like, as well as agitation and fear;
and the death of those related to oneself, caused by the loss of desired objects. (41)
If the lord of the second house is less than two [years old], there will be affliction of the body;
to ward off that evil, one should perform worship of the Sun.
When the Moon has entered the sign of Mercury and is endowed with the aspect of Jupiter, situated in its exaltation, its own sign, a quadrant, a trine, or even in the eleventh house; || 43 ||
If the [ascendant] is full and conjoined with auspicious planets, there is the attainment of the king's favor;
through the grace of the great king, one obtains vehicles, garments, and ornaments. 44.
There shall be good fortune, the increase of happiness, the protection of servants, well-being for the families of one's father and mother, and the auspicious increase of livestock. (45)
Or when [the Moon] is waned, or conjoined with a malefic, or aspected by a malefic, or situated in its sign of debilitation, or placed in a malefic navāṃśa, or even gone to a malefic house; || 46 ||
For one born under Jātaka, there is great suffering, royal wrath, loss of wealth, separation from father and mother, and afflictions caused by diseases of daughters, sons, and others. (47)
The fruit is not obtained through mere exertion; there is expenditure of wealth on various paths, as well as eating at improper times and the consumption of medicine [at the wrong time]. (48)

One should know this to be the result: happiness at the outset and the arrival of wealth, when [the planet] is situated in a quadrant (kendrā), a trine (trikoṇa), or the eleventh house from the lord of the period (dāyeśa). (49)
There is an increase in vehicles, clothing, livestock, and so forth, as well as prosperity from brothers, which brings happiness;
there is the attainment of happiness for one's father and mother, as well as marital bliss and the arrival of wealth. (50)

If the lord of the twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa, or the lord of the eighth house, is devoid of strength, it indicates desired happiness and auspiciousness through the influence of friends and masters.

One shall encounter bedridden illness, laziness, displacement from one's position, and the loss of happiness; furthermore, one will meet with the increase of enemies, hostility, and hatred from kinsmen. (52)
If the lord of the second house is deficient [in strength], bodily laziness will occur;
and for the sake of pacifying that defect, one should perform oblations of sesame seeds and other such rites.
One should give jaggery, ghee, rice smeared with curd, and according to the prescribed rite,
a white cow or a buffalo for the increase of longevity and health.

When Mars has entered the period of Saturn and is situated in a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine, or is in its exaltation or its own sign, and is conjoined with the lord of the [current] dasa; || 55 ||
When [the Moon] is conjoined with the lord of the ascendant, there is initially happiness and the arrival of wealth;
there is the favor of the king, happiness, and [the acquisition of] vehicles, garments, and ornaments. (56)

Generalship, the favor of the king, abundance of agriculture, cattle, and grain, the construction of new dwellings, and the attainment of desired happiness from one's circle of brothers [will result]. (57)
If Mars is heliacally set, situated in the eighth or twelfth house from the ascendant,
or even conjoined with or aspected by malefic planets, there will be loss of wealth.
There will be suffering from thieves, snakes, wounds, weapons, and the like, as well as from glandular diseases and other ailments;
there will be affliction caused by brothers, father, and others, and conflict with kinsmen. (59)
There will be loss of four-footed livestock, the eating of contemptible food, travel to foreign lands, and the expenditure of wealth on the wrong path. || 60 ||
If the lord of the eighth house is situated in the second house, or if it is otherwise [in that position],
there will indeed be fear of untimely death, various afflictions, and defeat.
To avoid those defects, one should perform a propitiatory fire-offering (śāntihoma) and make a gift of a bull,
which wards off all misfortunes.
When Rāhu is within the sphere of Saturn, there will be quarrels,
mental anguish, physical suffering, mental distress, hatred toward one's children, and fear of disease.
Expenditure of wealth, fear of the king, opposition from one's own kinsmen and others, travel to foreign lands, and the destruction of houses, fields, and so forth. (64)

When [the Moon] is conjoined with the lord of the ascendant, joined with a yoga-producing planet, situated in its exaltation or its own sign in a quadrant, and placed in the eleventh house from the lord of the period; || 65 ||

In the beginning, one shall obtain happiness, the acquisition of wealth, prosperity such as houses and fields, devotion toward gods and Brahmins, and undertake pilgrimages to sacred fords and the like.
There will be the acquisition of four-footed animals and auspicious prosperity in the home;
however, in the middle [period], there will be fear of the king and conflict with sons and friends. (67)
One should predict the attainment of sovereignty over elephants when [the Moon] is in Aries, Virgo, Cancer, Taurus, Pisces, Sagittarius, or Leo. (68)

It brings about the attainment of royal honor and ornaments, and produces the pleasure of soft enjoyments; however, if it is conjoined with the lords of the second and seventh houses, there will be affliction of the body. (69)
One should perform the Mṛtyuñjaya rite and cause the gift of medicine to be given;
one should also perform the gift of a bull, which brings about all prosperity and happiness.
When Jupiter is within the period of Saturn, and is situated in a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine, conjoined with the lord of the ascendant, or is in its exaltation or its own sign; || 71 ||
The accomplishment of all purposes will surely come to pass;
through the favor of the great king, there shall be wealth, vehicles, and ornaments.
There will be honor and the respect of masters, the acquisition of pleasant clothing and wealth, devotion to the deities and gurus, and association with learned people. (73)

There will be the acquisition of a wife, sons, and the like, as well as the prosperity of virtuous children, when Jupiter is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, or is debilitated, or conjoined with malefic planets. (74)
There will be the death of one's own relatives, the destruction of wealth and grain, public enmity toward the king, and the failure of undertakings. (75)

Furthermore, there will be travel to foreign lands and the occurrence of diseases such as leprosy, if [the Moon] is in a quadrant (kendram), a trine (koṇa), the second house, or even the eleventh house from the lord of the Dasa. || 76 ||
There shall be prosperity, the good fortune of a spouse, royal splendor, abundance of wealth, comfort from food and clothing, and the practice of charity and other virtuous deeds. (77)
The attainment of the foundation of Brahman, as well as the fruit of sacrificial rites, the gift of food, great renown, and the hearing of the Vedānta and so forth [are obtained]. (78)
If the lord of the eighth house is devoid of strength and situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa,
there will be enmity with kinsmen, mental anguish, quarrels, and loss of position.
There will be poor food, loss of livelihood, expenditure of wealth due to royal punishment, entry into prison, and suffering for one's wife, children, and others. (80)
But if the lord of the second house is deficient by two [degrees], there will be affliction of the body and mental anguish;
death related to oneself will occur, without a doubt. (81)
To avoid that fault, one should recite the *Śivasāhasraka*;
one should also perform the gift of gold, for health will certainly be attained.
Now begins the chapter on the results of the sub-periods (antardaśā) of Mercury. || 58 ||
The acquisition of pearls and coral, as well as knowledge, action, happiness, and the like;
the greatness of learning, fame, and the sight of a new sovereign. || 1 ||

Wealth consisting of wife, children, and so forth, which brings happiness to one's father and mother, [is obtained] when [the lord of the second house] is in its own exaltation and so on; however, it is lost when [that lord] is in its sign of debilitation, set (in the seventh), or situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house. || 2 ||

If [the lord of the ascendant] is conjoined with or aspected by a malefic, there will be loss of wealth, grain, and cattle, as well as conflict with oneself and one's kinsmen, and the occurrence of ailments such as colic pain. || 3 ||
He will certainly become overwhelmed by the multitude of royal duties;
however, if the lord of the second house is devoid of strength, there will be suffering regarding his wife.
Upon the death of a relative or the occurrence of wind-pain and other ailments,
one should recite the Viṣṇusahasraka for the purpose of removing those defects.

When Ketu is in the sub-period of Mercury and is situated in a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant, conjoined with benefics, aspected by benefics, and associated with the lord of the ascendant; || 6 ||

In the conjunction of the Yogakāraka with the lord of the Dasa situated in a quadrant or the eleventh house from it, one should predict physical comfort, meager wealth, and affection for kinsmen. || 7 ||
There will be the acquisition of four-footed animals, the arrival of wealth through travel,
engagement with learning and fame, and an audience with an equal sovereign.
Indeed, there will be happiness from food and clothing at the beginning [of the period], and it brings comfort in the middle;
however, if the lord of the dasa is situated in the eighth or twelfth house and is conjoined with malefic planets, [the results will be otherwise]. //9//
There is falling from one's vehicle, the occurrence of suffering for one's children and so forth, and constant fear of thieves and the king; such a person is always intent upon sinful deeds.

There will be fear of the venom of scorpions and the like, the occurrence of quarrels with base people, and suffering such as grief and disease, arising from association with the low-born and similar causes. (11)
If the lord of the second house is less than two [signs] away, there will be physical lethargy;
to remedy that defect, one should perform the gift of medicine. || 12 ||

When Venus enters the sub-period of Mercury, if it is situated in a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine, there is an accumulation of noble discourse, merit, and dharma, and one performs virtuous deeds. (13)
Through the influence of a friendly planet, the desired acquisition of land and happiness shall occur,
provided that [the planet] is situated in a quadrant, a trine, or the eleventh house from the lord of the period.
At that time, one attains prosperity, royal glory, and abundance of wealth;
this includes the undertaking of meritorious acts such as the construction of step-wells, wells, and tanks.

If the lord of the Dasa is situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from the lord of the Mahadasa and is devoid of strength, there will be an abundance of effort resulting in an excess of fruit, yet it will cause a depletion of wealth and grain.
Heart disease, loss of honor, suffering from fever and dysentery, and separation from oneself and one's kinsmen—these certainly occur in this worldly existence. (17)
O best of the twice-born, it brings personal hardship and mental anguish;
moreover, when the lord [of the ascendant] is diminished by two [degrees], untimely death will occur.
To avoid those defects, one should perform the recitation (japa) of the goddess Durgā;
through the grace of the Mother of the World, one shall then attain peace. || 19 ||

When the Sun enters the sub-period of Saumya, and is situated in its exaltation, its own sign, a quadrant, a trine, or in the second or eleventh house, or at its degree of exaltation, or even in its own Navāṃśa; || 20 ||

When [the Moon] is aspected by the son of the Earth (Mars) at the beginning, one should predict good fortune from the favor of the king, happiness through the influence of friends and lords, and the initial acquisition of land.

When [the Moon] is aspected by the lord of the ascendant, it brings great happiness, the arrival of wealth, the acquisition of villages, land, and so forth, and provides the comfort of food and clothing. (22)

Or if [the lord of the Dasa] is in the eighth or twelfth house from the Ascendant, conjoined with Saturn, Mars, or Rahu; or if it is situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa, being devoid of strength. (23)
There will be suffering from weapons such as those used by thieves, an excess of bile (pitta), and mental anguish caused by the separation from beloved kinsmen. (24)
If the lord of the second or the seventh house is [the Moon], untimely death will occur;
to ward off that evil, one should perform a propitiatory rite according to the prescribed rules.

When the Moon enters the sub-period of Mercury, and the Moon is situated in a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant, or in its own exaltation, or in its own sign, and is endowed with the aspect of Jupiter; || 26 ||
One should predict the intensity of yoga by the predominance of its constituent factors;
it brings the acquisition of a wife, the birth of a son, and [the gain of] clothing, vehicles, and ornaments. (27)
The acquisition of a new dwelling, the constant enjoyment of sweet foods, engagement in song and instrumental music, and diligent application to the study of the sciences and scriptures. (28)
Taking recourse to the southern direction, there will be a journey;
furthermore, there will be the acquisition of garments from other islands and such places. || 29 ||
One shall obtain pearls, coral, gems, washed garments, and so forth; however, when conjoined with a base *ari-kṣetra*, there will be affliction of the body. (30)
If Duścikya is situated in a quadrant (kendraka), a trine (koṇa), or in the eleventh house from the lord of the Mahādaśā,
then at the commencement of its sub-period (bhukti) and so forth, there will be a vision of holy pilgrimage sites, sacred places, and deities.
There will be mental fortitude, enthusiasm in the heart, and the acquisition of wealth from abroad;
however, if [the lord of the ascendant] is joined by malefic planets in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa, [these results will not come to pass].
There will be fear of thieves, fire, and kings arising from association with women;
there will be misconduct, loss of wealth, and the destruction of crops, cattle, horses, and other possessions. (33)
If the lord of the second house is deficient [in strength], there will be affliction of the body;
to remedy that defect, one should perform the recitation (japa) of the goddess Durgā.
One should perform the gift of clothing, which brings about the increase of longevity and happiness;
through the grace of the Mother of the World, one shall thereafter attain bliss. (35)

When Mars enters the sub-period of Mercury, and is situated in a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant, or in its own exaltation, or in its own sign, or conjoined with the lord of the ascendant; || 36 ||
One who has lost their kingdom shall obtain the king's favor, peace, the occurrence of auspiciousness in the home, and the signs of Lakṣmī’s favorable glance. (37)
The joy of festivals for one's sons and so forth, an abundance of cattle and wealth in the home, the acquisition of houses, fields, and the like, together with elephants and horses. (38)
It brings delight to the king and exceedingly beautiful happiness from women, even when situated in the eighth or the twelfth house in a lowly sign. (39)
Or if it is conjoined with a malefic aspect, there will be affliction of the body and mental anguish;
at the beginning of the period, there will be a failure of enterprise and the loss of grain in one's own village.

There is fear of tumors, weapons, wounds, and the like, as well as the affliction of fever and other ailments, when Mars is in a quadrant, a trine, or the eleventh house from the lord of the Mahādaśā. (41)
When the aspect is auspicious, men shall obtain wealth and bodily comfort;
there will be the gain of sons, an increase in fame, and a very dear circle of brothers. (42)
If the lord of the eighth house is situated in the eighth or the twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa, or is conjoined with malefic planets,
there will be great suffering at the commencement of that Dasa's sub-period, and great fear regarding the circle of brothers.
There will be fear of kings, fire, and thieves, as well as conflict with sons and friends;
initially there will be displacement from one's position, but in the middle [of the period] there will be happiness and the arrival of wealth.
But before that, there may be fear of the king or even displacement from one's position;
if the lord of the second house is also debilitated, there will be fear of untimely death.
One should perform the gift of a cow and practice the recitation of the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra;
through the grace of Śaṅkara, one will thereafter attain a happy death.
When Rāhu enters the sub-period (antardaśā) of Mercury, and is situated in a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine, or in Cancer, Aquarius, Virgo, or Taurus; || 47 ||
There will arise honor from the king, fame, and wealth;
likewise, there will be the attainment of sacred pilgrimage sites and the vision of deities.
One should predict that there will be the performance of sacrifices and charitable works, great honor, and the acquisition of clothing;
however, at the beginning of the period there will be bodily affliction during eating and other activities, while at the end there will be happiness. (49)
When [the Moon] is situated in the eighth or twelfth house from the ascendant, there is loss of wealth during its transit;
at the beginning of the transit, there is danger to the body, and it causes wind-fever and indigestion.
If Rāhu is in an upacaya house from the ascendant and is conjoined with a benefic planet, there will be satisfaction from conversation with the king and an audience with a new sovereign. (51)
If the lord of the Dāya is in the twelfth or the eighth house, conjoined with malefic planets,
there will be harsh royal duties, as well as loss of position and great fear.
There will be imprisonment, affliction by disease, mental anguish for one's own kinsmen, heart disease, loss of honor, and loss of wealth. (53)
If [the planet] is situated in the second or the seventh house, untimely death (apamṛtyu) will indeed occur;
to ward off that evil, one should perform the recitation of the Durgā-lakṣmī mantra.
One should give a white cow or a buffalo that bestows long life and health;
through the grace of the Mother of the World, one shall thereafter attain happiness. || 55 ||
When Jupiter enters the sub-period of Mercury and is situated in a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant, or in its own exaltation, its own sign, or in the eleventh or second house; || 56 ||
Physical well-being, the acquisition of wealth, and likewise the favor of kings; marriage festivities and ceremonies, and the constant enjoyment of sweet foods. (57)
The acquisition of cows, buffaloes, and so forth; the listening to the Purāṇas and other such activities;
devotion to the deities and the guru; and the practice of charity, religious duty, sacrifice, and the like. (58)

The prosperity of sacrificial rites as well as the fruit of the worship of Śiva [is attained] even when [the planet] is in its sign of debilitation, set, or placed in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house. (59)
When conjoined with the aspect of Saturn or Mars, there will be quarrels, conflict with the king, bodily afflictions from thieves and the like, and the death of one's father or mother. (60)

There will be loss of honor, royal punishment, and loss of wealth; furthermore, there will be suffering from poison, snakes, and fever, as well as the destruction of fields and agricultural lands. (61)

If [the lord of the third house] is in a quadrant, a trine, or the eleventh house from the lord of the day, being endowed with strength, there will be enthusiasm for kinsmen and children, as well as auspiciousness and the acquisition of wealth. (62)

The increase of cattle, the increase of fame, and the fruit of giving food and other gifts [occur] when the lord of the Dāya (the year-lord) is devoid of strength and situated in the sixth, the eighth, or the twelfth house.
There will be fever in the limbs, physical infirmity, bodily affliction, discord with wife and kinsmen, royal wrath, and loss of wealth. (64)
There will be fear of sudden quarrels, negligence, and danger from twice-born men;
or else, if [the planet] is situated in the second or seventh house, there will be physical affliction. (65)
To avoid those defects, one should recite the *Śivasāhasraka*;
by the gift of cows, land, and gold, one dispels all misfortunes.

When Saturn enters the sub-period of Mercury, if it is situated in its exaltation, its own sign, a quadrant, a trine, or the eleventh house, there will be an increase in auspiciousness within the home.
The attainment of a kingdom, great energy, and a home filled with wealth in cattle. || 68 ||

One should likewise predict the attainment of results from auspicious places and residence at sacred fords (tīrtha) when Saturn is in the eighth or the twelfth house from the lord of the dasa, or similarly from the lord of the dasa itself.
Abundance of enemies and suffering, affliction from wife, children, and others, loss of intellect, destruction of kinsmen, ruin of one's undertakings, and mental anguish. (70)
There will be travel abroad as well as the appearance of bad dreams and the like;
moreover, if the lord of the second house is devoid of strength, an untimely death (apamṛtyu) will occur.
To avoid those defects, one should perform the recitation of the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra;
one should give a black cow or a buffalo for the increase of longevity and health.
Now begins the chapter on the results of the sub-periods (antardaśā) of Ketu. 59.

If Ketu is in the tenth house, a trine, or the eleventh house, conjoined with the lord of the ascendant, or associated with the ninth or tenth houses, or joined with the lord of the fourth house; || 1 ||

During its period, it brings wealth, grain, and so forth; it causes the acquisition of four-footed animals and living beings, as well as happiness from children and wife, favor from the king, and mental anguish. (2)

There will be the acquisition of villages, lands, and so forth, as well as a house filled with wealth in the form of cattle, even when [the lord of the ascendant] is joined by a planet in its sign of debilitation, its setting, or placed in the eighth or the twelfth house. || 3 ||
Heart disease, loss of honor, the depletion of wealth, grain, and cattle, suffering for wife and children, and indeed mental instability; || 4 ||
If a relationship exists there with the lord of the second house minus one,
great ill-health and severe suffering arise, causing separation from oneself and one's kinsmen.
One should perform the recitation (japa) of Durgādevī and practice the recitation of Mṛtyuñjaya;
thus, when Ketu has entered one's own [ascendant], one shall thereafter attain happiness.

When Venus has entered Ketu’s sign, is in its exaltation, or conjoined with its own domicile, or is situated in a quadrant, a trine, or the eleventh house, or is joined with the lord of the ninth house; || 7 ||
It bestows royal favor and good fortune, filled with fine garments;
at that time, one attains prosperity when it is conjoined with the lords of fortune and action.
The recovery of a lost kingdom and wealth, the attainment of excellent happiness and vehicles,
as well as the bathing at the Setu and the great vision of the deity.
Through the favor of the great king, one obtains villages, land, and so forth,
if [the lord of the year] is in a quadrant (kendraka), a trine (koṇa), the second house, or the eleventh house from the lord of the dasa.
It brings physical health and auspiciousness, as well as prosperity and beauty within the home;
it grants the acquisition of food, clothing, and ornaments, and bestows the gain of chariots, palanquins, and other such luxuries.
If [the Moon] is situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa, or is conjoined with malefic planets,
there will be sudden quarrels as well as affliction to livestock, grain, and other possessions.

If [the lord of the ascendant] is situated in its sign of debilitation, conjoined with a planet, or located in the sixth or eighth house from the ascendant, there will be discord with one's own kinsmen and suffering from wounds to the head and eyes. (13)
One should predict heart disease, loss of honor, the depletion of wealth, grain, and cattle, as well as the occurrence of suffering for one's wife and children. (14)
If the lord of the second house is less than two [years old], there will be physical lethargy and mental affliction;
to remedy those defects, one should perform the recitation (japa) of the goddess Durgā.
For the increase of longevity and health, one should give away a white cow or a buffalo. || 15 ||

When the Sun is situated within Ketu's sign, or even when it is in its exaltation or its own sign, or in a quadrant, a trine, or the eleventh house, being conjoined with or aspected by benefic planets; || 16 ||
There will be the acquisition of wealth, grain, and so forth, as well as the majesty of royal favor; many auspicious undertakings and the attainment of desired goals shall bring happiness. (17)
When the eighth house is an expenditure sign (vyayārāśi) and is occupied by malefic planets,
there is fear of the king during its period, and it causes separation from one's father and mother.
There will be travel abroad, suffering from thieves, snakes, and poison, opposition from the king and friends, and loss of wealth due to royal punishment. (19)
There will be grief, disease, fear, excessive heat, and fever,
if [the Moon] is situated in the tenth, eleventh, fifth, or second house from the lord of the Dasa.
There will be physical comfort, gain of wealth, acquisition of sons, and firmness of mind;
there shall be success in all undertakings and purposes, accompanied by lordship over a small village.
If the lord of the eighth house from the lord of the Mahādaśā is situated in the eighth or twelfth house, or is conjoined with malefic planets,
there will be obstacles in obtaining food, mental distress, and the loss of wealth, grain, and cattle.
One should predict great affliction at the beginning and middle, and happiness at the end;
for if the lord of the second or seventh house [is afflicted], untimely death will surely occur.
One should perform a propitiatory rite for him and cause a golden cow to be given;
then, by the grace of the Sun, he shall obtain happiness. (24)
When the Moon has entered Ketu, or is in its exaltation or its own sign, or is in a quadrant, a trine, or the eleventh house, or in the second house conjoined with a benefic; || 25 ||
Affection from the king, great energy, auspiciousness, and great happiness;
through the grace of the great king, there is the acquisition of houses, land, and so forth. (26)
There is great fruit from undertakings concerning food, clothing, cattle, and the like;
as well as the acquisition of horses for riding, and the obtaining of garments, ornaments, and jewelry. (27)
The Full Moon bestows the accumulation of merit and dharma through temples, tanks, and so forth, as well as the happiness of children, wife, and other such blessings. (28)
Or if the Moon is waned, debilitated, or situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, there will be loss of personal happiness, mental anguish, obstacles to one's work, and great fear. (29)
One should predict separation from father and mother, physical lethargy, mental anguish, the bitter fruit of one's efforts, the loss of cattle, and fear. (30)

If [the lord of the year] is in a quadrant (kendraka), a trine (koṇa), or the eleventh house (lābha) from the lord of the year, and is endowed with strength, there will be gain of agriculture, cattle, and land, as well as the meeting with beloved kinsmen. || 31 ||
Therefore, the accomplishment of one's own purpose, cow's milk in the home, auspiciousness at the beginning of meals, health, and being favored by the king in the middle [of life] are attained. (32)
But at the beginning [of the year], there is fear of the king, as well as travel to foreign lands, wandering on long journeys, and honoring one's kinsmen. (33)
If the lord of the Dasa is devoid of strength and situated in the sixth, twelfth, or eighth house from the Moon,
there will be loss of wealth, grain, and so forth, as well as mental distress and family strife.
There will be enmity with one's own kinsmen and likewise suffering caused by brothers,
due to the defect of the lord of the eighth house being conjoined with the lord of the second or seventh house.
One should perform the pacification of his fear of untimely death according to the prescribed rite, as well as that which pleases the Moon, for the sake of attaining long life and health. (36)
When Mars is situated within Ketu's period, occupying a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant, or being in its exaltation or its own sign, and joined with or aspected by benefic planets; || 37 ||
In the beginning, there is indeed an auspicious result, bringing the acquisition of villages, lands, and so forth;
as well as the gain of wealth, grain, and the like, and the acquisition of four-footed living beings. || 38 ||

The acquisition of houses, gardens, and fields, as well as the power of royal favor, and the gain of land and happiness itself occur when there is a connection between the lord of the tenth house and the lord of the ninth house. || 39 ||

If [the lord of the year] is in a quadrant, a trine, the second house, or the eleventh house from the lord of the Dasa, it brings favor from the king, the acquisition of fame, and happiness through sons, friends, and others. (40)
Likewise, when Mars is in the eighth or the twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa, or even in the second house from him,
it swiftly causes death in a foreign land, as well as calamity and wandering.
It brings urinary disorders, dysuria, and afflictions from thieves and the like, as well as trouble from kings; it involves quarrels and pain, yet increases some degree of happiness. (42)
If the lord of the second house is less than two [years old], there will be fear of fever, distress, poison, and danger;
there will be suffering for the wife, mental anguish, and the fear of untimely death. || 43 ||
One should indeed give a draught-ox, which brings about all prosperity and happiness;
through that, one attains peace by the grace of the planet Mars.

When Rāhu is within Ketu's [sign], situated in its own exaltation, in a friendly sign or its own sign, in a quadrant (kendraka), a trine (trikoṇa), the eleventh house (lābha), or in the second or seventh house (duścikya-dhanasaṃjñaka); || 45 ||
At that time, there will be gain of wealth and movement will certainly occur;
through the power of a Mleccha lord, there will be happiness and an abundance of grain, fruits, and so forth.

There will be the acquisition of four-footed animals and the gain of villages, land, and so forth; one experiences distress at the beginning of the period of enjoyment, but shall obtain happiness at its middle and end. (47)
If Rāhu is in the eighth or the twelfth house, conjoined with or aspected by malefic planets, there will be excessive urination, emaciation, tallness, and fear from cold fever and poison. (48)
One should predict quartan fever, affliction by minor calamities, sudden quarrels, urinary disorders, and colic pain. (49)
If [the Moon] is situated in the second or the seventh house, then there will be affliction and great fear;
for the purpose of avoiding those defects, one should perform the recitation (japa) of the goddess Durgā.

When Jupiter is situated within Ketu's division, placed in a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine, or is in its exaltation or its own sign, and is conjoined with the lord of the ascendant; || 51 ||
When [the Moon] is conjoined with the lords of Karma, Bhāgya, and Ādhipati, it bestows wealth, grain, and the attainment of riches;
furthermore, it grants royal favor, enthusiasm, horses, swings, and the like.
In the home, there shall be the attainment of auspicious prosperity, the birth of sons, great festivals,
visits to holy pilgrimage sites, great enthusiasm, and virtuous deeds that bring happiness.
Through the grace of one's chosen deity, there will be victory, the accomplishment of tasks, and gain;
there will be conversations with kings, performance of duties, and an audience with a new sovereign. (54)
If Jupiter is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa, even if it is in its sign of debilitation,
there will be fear of thieves, snakes, and wounds, as well as the destruction of wealth, grain, and other possessions.
One should declare that there will be separation from children and wife, arising from extreme suffering;
though it yields auspicious results at first, it brings distress in the end. (56)

If [the lord of the year] is in a quadrant, a trine, the second house, or the eleventh house from the lord of the Dasa, and is joined with a benefic, there will be the favor of the king and various garments and ornaments. (57)
Traveling to distant lands, the maintenance of one's own kinsmen, food, clothing, livestock, and so forth, as well as physical suffering during the enjoyment of these things; 58.
If [the lord of the second house] is in the first house, there will be a sudden displacement from one's position and quarrels;
however, if the lord of the second house is in the eighth house, premature death will occur.
To avoid those defects, one should recite the *Śivasāhasraka*;
the recitation of the *Mahāmṛtyuñjaya* destroys all calamities. (60)
When Saturn enters Ketu's [sub-period] during its own major period, there is suffering, distress for kinsmen, mental anguish, and the acquisition of four-footed animals. 61.
Through a multitude of royal affairs, there will be loss of wealth and great fear;
there shall be displacement from one's position, exile, and danger from thieves on the road. (62)
In the eighth house, when Saturn is situated in the sign of expenditure (the twelfth), there is laziness and loss of mental vigor;
likewise, when Saturn is in its trine in Pisces, or in its own sign in Libra. (63)

If [the planet] is in the tenth, fifth, or eleventh house, or in the second or seventh house, or in a benefic division (navāṃśa), and is aspected by or joined with benefics, there is the accomplishment of all undertakings and purposes. || 64 ||
There is great happiness from one's own master, and wandering about brings joy;
there is the attainment of happiness in one's own village and the sight of the king within one's own circle. 65.
If the lord of the Dasa is in the sixth, twelfth, or eighth house, or is conjoined with malefic planets,
there will be physical suffering, mental anguish, obstacles in one's work, and great fear.
If the lord of the second house is deficient [in strength], there will be laziness, loss of honor, the destruction of one's father and mother,
and indeed the fear of untimely death.
To eliminate those defects, one should perform an oblation of sesame seeds;
furthermore, for the increase of longevity and health, one should donate a black cow or a buffalo.

When Mercury is situated within Ketu's Navamsha, occupying a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine, and is in its exaltation or its own sign, there is the attainment of kingship and great happiness. (69)
Listening to virtuous discourses, generosity, and the accomplishment of Dharma bring happiness;
there is the gain of land, the birth of a son, auspicious assemblies, and the arrival of wealth. (70)
There will be the effortless attainment of dharma and marriage;
in the home, there will be auspicious rites and the adorning with garments and ornaments.
When joined with the lords of fortune and karma, there will be an increase in fortune that brings happiness;
and through conversations in the assemblies of the learned, time will be spent meaningfully. (72)
If Mercury is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, conjoined with or aspected by Saturn,
Mars, or Rahu, there will be conflict with royal officials and residence in another's house.
It causes the destruction of vehicles, clothing, livestock, wealth, grain, and so forth;
yet it is said to be auspicious at the beginning of its period, while in the middle there is happiness and the arrival of wealth. (74)

Furthermore, there will be affliction from one's wife and children as well as the onset of mental distress, provided that a benefic planet is situated in a quadrant, a trine, or the eleventh house from the lord of the Dasa. (75)
Health of the body is a great gain, as is the splendor of virtuous sons;
food, clothing, cattle, and so forth are the abundant fruits of one's professional endeavors.
If the lord of the eighth house is devoid of strength and situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa,
there will be great suffering at the commencement of that Dasa, along with affliction to one's wife, children, and others.
He will cause fear from kings and become a heretic in the middle [of his life];
however, if the lord of the second house is deficient, there will indeed be an untimely death.
To avoid those faults, one should recite the Viṣṇusahasraka;
thereafter, by the grace of Śrī Hari, one attains happiness. (79)
Now begins the chapter on the results of the sub-periods of Venus. 60.

Now, if Venus is within one's own [sign] and situated in a quadrant (kendr), a trine (trikoṇa), or the eleventh house from the ascendant, and is endowed with strength, its period yields auspicious results. || 1 ||

The acquisition of wealth from Brahmins, the gain of cattle, buffaloes, and the like, joy through the birth of a son and other festivities, and the occurrence of auspicious events within the home. (2)
There is honor, royal recognition, the attainment of a kingdom, and great happiness, when [the planet] is in its exaltation, its own sign, its exaltation degree, or even its own division. || 3 ||
The construction of a new dwelling, the constant eating of sweet foods, the prosperity of wife and sons, and dining together with friends. || 4 ||

The giving of food is always dear to him; he gathers wealth through the practice of charity and other virtues; and by the grace of the great king, he possesses vehicles, garments, and ornaments. || 5 ||
From perseverance comes an abundance of results; it brings gain from four-footed creatures and life.
In the western part, there is travel that brings the acquisition of vehicles and garments.

When Venus is in an upacaya house from the ascendant or other, conjoined with or aspected by benefic planets, situated in a friendly navāṃśa, or in its exaltation, its sign of gain (lābha-rāśi), or in a yoga involving its lord, it brings prosperity. || 7 ||
The attainment of a kingdom, great enthusiasm, and the king’s favor bringing auspiciousness; the abundance of blessings in the home and the increase of wife, sons, and so forth. || 8 ||
If Venus is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, conjoined with or aspected by malefic planets,
there is fear of wounds from thieves and the like, and suffering for all people everywhere.
There will be hatred from the people at the royal gate, the destruction of beloved kinsmen, suffering for one's wife and children, and oppression of the populace everywhere. (10)
If death should occur while the lord of the second house is situated in the eighth house, one should perform the recitation of the Durgā mantra and cause the gift of a bow to be made. || 11 ||
When the Sun enters the sub-period of Venus, there is suffering, conflict with the king,
and quarrels with kinsmen, provided it is neither in its exaltation nor its depression.

When the Sun is in the sub-period of Venus, there is distress caused by kings, strife, and quarrels with kinsmen; however, if it is situated in a benefic sign or a trine, these evils are absent. When the Sun is in its exaltation, in its own sign, in a friendly sign, or in a quadrant or a trine, [the results are auspicious].
If [the lord of the year] is in a quadrant, a trine, the eleventh house, or even the second house from the lord of the year; || 13 ||
During its period, there shall be gain of wealth, as well as sovereignty, women, and riches; furthermore, there will be great happiness from one's own master and reunion with beloved kinsmen. (14)
He attains the happiness of his father and mother, the acquisition of brothers which brings joy, good reputation, happiness, good fortune, and the birth of a son. || 15 ||
Likewise, if the Sun is in the eighth house, or in the twelfth, or situated in the sign of an enemy,
or in its sign of debilitation, or in the division of a malefic, there will be physical suffering and mental anguish.
There is constant affliction from one's own kin, perpetual harsh speech, suffering for one's father, loss of kinsmen, and causing opposition at the royal court. (17)
There will be suffering from wounds, affliction by snakes, as well as fear within one's own home;
furthermore, there will be fear of various diseases and the destruction of houses, fields, and so forth. (18)
If the Sun is the lord of the seventh house, there will be affliction from the planets;
for the sake of averting that evil, one should perform rites to propitiate the Sun. || 19 ||

When the Moon enters the sub-period of Venus and is situated in a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine; or when it is in its exaltation or its own sign, conjoined with the lord of the ninth house; || 20 ||
When the full moon is conjoined with a benefic planet and associated with the lord of the ninth house (rājyanātha),
or when that [lord] is in its own sign (tadbuktau), there is the acquisition of vehicles and the like, as well as great happiness in the home.
By the grace of the Great King, one may attain the sovereignty of the lord of elephants;
[one gains] the merit of bathing in a great river and the worship of gods and Brahmins.

Devotion to singing, instrumental music, and the like, as well as the prosperity of cows, buffaloes, and other livestock, are the superior fruits of one's industrious efforts, which adorn the wise. (23)
There is comfort from food and clothing, as well as meals shared with kinsmen,
when [the Moon] is in its sign of debilitation, or in its own or exaltation sign, or situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house.
If [the lord of the year] is situated in the sixth, the eighth, or the twelfth house from the lord of the year,
there will be loss of wealth at that time, and great fear shall prevail.
Physical exhaustion, mental anguish, opposition at the king’s gate, travel to foreign lands, and pilgrimages to sacred sites are the resulting fruits. (26)

There will be suffering for one's wife, children, and others, as well as separation from one's own kinsmen, if [the Moon] is situated in a quadrant (kendram), the eleventh house, a trine (trikoṇa), or the third house from the lord of the Mahādaśā. || 27 ||
It brings delight to kings, as well as lordship over countries and villages;
it confers fortitude, fame, happiness, renown, vehicles, garments, and ornaments. (28)

The construction of wells, gardens, tanks, and the like, as well as the accumulation of wealth, may bring physical comfort at the beginning of one's enjoyment, but in the end, there will likewise be suffering. (29)

During the sub-period of Mars within the major period of Venus, if Mars is situated in a quadrant or a trine from the ascendant, or is in its exaltation, its own sign, or in the eleventh house, endowed with strength. || 30 ||
If [the Moon] is conjoined with the lord of the ascendant, or conjoined with the lords of the tenth and ninth houses,
one should predict excellent prosperity, such as royal yoga, during its period.
The attainment of desired objects such as clothing, ornaments, land, and so forth brings happiness;
this is likewise the case when [the lord of the Dasa] is in the eighth or the twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa. (32)

There will be suffering from cold fevers and the like, fear brought about by one's father and mother, diseases such as fever that are aggravated, displacement from one's position, and mental anguish. (33)
There will be loss of one's own kinsmen, quarrels, and conflict with the king; there will be hatred from people at the royal court and excessive expenditure of wealth and grain. (34)
If the lord of the second house is weak, the desired fruit from one's efforts will not be attained due to the loss of village lands and such;
however, if the lord of the second house is in the twelfth house, there will be affliction to the body.

When Rāhu is in the sub-period of Venus and is situated in a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine, or in its own exaltation, aspected by benefics, and conjoined with a yoga-kāraka planet; || 36 ||
During its period, there will be great happiness and the acquisition of wealth, grain, and other assets;
one should predict a residence filled with beloved kinsmen.
For one who travels, there shall be the accomplishment of his purpose and the acquisition of cattle, fields, and so forth;
when Rāhu is in an upacaya house from the ascendant, its transit will bring happiness.

It brings the destruction of enemies, great energy, and is auspicious, pleasing to the king; at the beginning of its enjoyment it lasts for five months, and at the end it causes fever and indigestion. (39)
He encounters obstacles to his undertakings and mental distress while traveling, yet he enjoys supreme happiness and good fortune like a great king. || 40 ||
If one sets out toward the southwest (naiṛtī) direction, there will be a vision of the Lord;
for the traveler, there shall be success in his purpose, and he will return again to his own country.
If the lord of the ninth house is situated in the eighth or the twelfth house, conjoined with malefic planets, it results in service to Brahmins and the fruit of visiting sacred pilgrimage sites.
O best of the twice-born, he incurs inauspicious karma extending even to his father and mother, and suffers hatred from all people in various forms.
One should indicate the death of the body in the second or even the seventh [house];
for the sake of avoiding that defect, one should perform the recitation of the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra.

When Jupiter enters the sub-period of Venus, being situated in its exaltation, its own sign, or a quadrant, located in the third house from the lord of the major period, or in the ninth or fifth house; || 45 ||
A man shall regain a lost kingdom, obtain wealth, and acquire the abundance of desired objects and fine garments;
he shall receive honor from the lord of his friends, as well as riches and grain.
It brings honor and fame from royal patronage, the acquisition of horses, palanquins, and other such luxuries, and the diligent study of the scriptures in the company of learned masters. (47)

One should predict the joy of festivals such as the birth of a son, reunion with beloved kinsmen, the attainment of happiness from one's father and mother, and the well-being of children and other relatives. (48)

If the lord of the Dāya [year] is situated in the sixth or the twelfth house, or is conjoined with malefic planets, there will be suffering from kings, thieves, and the like, as well as physical affliction. (49)
There will be suffering for oneself and one's kinsmen, mental anguish due to quarrels, loss of position, exile, and one shall incur various diseases. (50)
If the lord of the second or the seventh house is [malefic], there will be affliction of the body;
for the sake of removing that defect, one should perform the Mahāmṛtyuñjaya rite.

When Saturn enters the sub-period of Venus, if it is in its own exaltation, its highest exaltation, situated in its own sign, a quadrant, a trine, or in its exaltation degree or its own Navamsha degree; || 52 ||
During its period, there will be great happiness, reunion with beloved kinsmen, honor at the royal court, and the birth of a daughter. (53)
One who performs meritorious deeds such as charity and dharma attains the fruits of sacred pilgrimage sites;
one attains the station of their own lord, but if [the planet] is situated in the eighth house, there will be suffering and misfortune.
Likewise, one suffers from physical lethargy and excessive expenditure when Saturn is in the eighth or the twelfth house from the ascendant or from the lord of the Dasa. (55)

At the beginning of the period of enjoyment and so forth, there is various suffering extending to one's father and mother, as well as affliction for one's wife and children, and wandering in foreign lands and the like. (56)
Due to exertion, the fruit [of one's efforts] will be lost, causing loss of cattle, buffaloes, and so forth;
if the lord of the second or the seventh house is [afflicted], there will be physical suffering.
To avoid those defects, one should perform an oblation of sesame seeds (tilahoma),
and should also perform the recitation of the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra or the chanting of the Caṇḍī.
Either by oneself or through a Brāhmaṇa, according to one's capacity and according to the prescribed rite, one then attains peace through the grace of Śiva and Śambhu. (59)

When Mercury enters the sub-period of Venus and is situated in a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine, or in its exaltation, or in its own sign, it brings about auspiciousness that wins the favor of the king. (60)
Good fortune, the birth of a son, the acquisition of wealth through righteous means, the hearing of the Purāṇic dharma, and association with amorous people. (61)
His palace was filled with beloved kinsmen and beautifully adorned;
he enjoyed great happiness from his own master and ate sweet food constantly. (62)
If the lord of the eighth house is devoid of strength and situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house from the lord of the Mahādaśā,
and is aspected by or conjoined with malefic planets, it causes the loss of four-footed animals.
Dwelling in another's house leads to the impairment of the mind;
in all undertakings, there is only loss, without a doubt. (64)
At the beginning of an enjoyment and so forth, it is said to be auspicious; in the middle, one should indicate middling results;
and at the end, it causes distress such as cold, wind, fever, and the like.
Due to the defect of the lord of the seventh house, bodily affliction will occur;
to remedy that defect, one should recite the Viṣṇusahasraka.
When Ketu enters the sub-period of Venus, whether it is situated in its exaltation or its own sign, and is connected with a yoga-maker planet while endowed with positional strength; || 67 ||
At the beginning of eating and other such activities, there will be auspiciousness due to abundance; one will constantly enjoy sweet foods.
Through business ventures, there will be an excess of fruits, and it will cause an increase in cattle, land, wealth, and so forth. (68)
There shall be an abundance of wealth and grain, and victory in battle;
at the end of the enjoyment there is indeed happiness, while at the beginning of the enjoyment the fruit is middling.
One should predict great suffering at intervals, followed by health,
when the lord of the Dasa is situated in the eighth or the twelfth house from the lord of the Dasa and is conjoined with malefic planets.
One should declare that there will be affliction from thieves, snakes, and wounds, loss of intellect, great fear, headache, mental distress, and quarrels over improper actions. (71)
There will be diseases arising from urinary disorders, expenditure of wealth through various channels, conflict with wife and sons, travel, and the ruin of undertakings. (72)
If the lord of the second house is less than two [years old], there will be affliction of the body;
to ward off that evil, one should perform the recitation of the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra.
One should perform the gift of liberality, which bestows all prosperity;
thereafter, one shall attain happiness through the peace that brings delight to Śukra.
